ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In digestive cancers, activating RAS mutations - primarily KRAS, less frequently NRAS - are among the most prevalent oncogenic drivers. Their clinical significance depends strongly on the tumor type, disease stage, treatment context, and specific RAS variant. In colorectal cancer (CRC), RAS alterations are well-established predictors of resistance to anti-EGFR therapy. However, KRAS G12C-mutant tumors represent a distinct subgroup with demonstrated sensitivity to KRAS G12C inhibitors. However, growing evidence supports the negative prognostic impact of RAS mutations on both primary CRC and colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) in both post-resection and adjuvant therapies. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), where KRAS alterations are nearly universal, prognostic evaluation has evolved from a binary mutant versus wild-type classification to a more refined approach based on mutation subtype (e.g., G12D/V vs. G12R) and KRAS mutant dosage, both of which influence clinical outcomes. In biliary tract cancers, KRAS mutations occur in a relevant subset and are consistently associated with poor survival. Liquid biopsy approaches increasingly enable noninvasive detection and longitudinal monitoring. In gastric cancer, RAS alterations are less frequent overall but may identify biologically aggressive subsets and may also be associated with inferior outcomes under HER2-targeted therapy in selected populations. This review synthesizes contemporary data supporting RAS alterations as prognostic biomarkers across digestive cancers, highlights practical considerations for integrating variant-level RAS information into risk stratification and trial designs, and discusses how emerging RAS-directed therapies may reshape the prognostic significance of specific molecular subsets.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anastomotic leakage after rectal resection may present months after surgery as a contained presacral collection. When an established defect communicates with the rectal lumen, endoscopic transanastomotic drainage can use that tract without creating a new transmural access route. We report a 54-year-old man who presented six months after anterior rectal resection with fever, pelvic pain, tenesmus, and purulent rectal discharge. Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging showed a multiloculated 6 × 5 × 2 cm presacral collection with a fistulous tract to the posterior colorectal anastomosis. Radial endoscopic ultrasonography measured a longest cavity dimension of 87.1 mm, and colonoscopy identified a draining posterior anastomotic defect. After intravenous antibiotic therapy was initiated, the defect was cannulated under colonoscopic and fluoroscopic guidance, the cavity was lavaged, and a 7-Fr × 7-cm double-pigtail plastic stent was deployed for internal drainage. Symptoms and inflammatory markers normalized within one week. At two months, a residual 40-mm cavity remained, and a second identical stent was placed alongside the first. At three months, the patient remained asymptomatic, but both stents were still in situ, and definitive cavity closure had not yet been documented. This case demonstrates the technical feasibility of transanastomotic drainage and short-term clinical control in a selected patient without peritoneal signs; it does not establish durable healing or generalizable efficacy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colonoscopy is a vital diagnostic and therapeutic procedure for diseases affecting the rectum, colon, and terminal ileum. In patients who have undergone colorectal surgery, postoperative colonoscopy is frequently required for purposes such as colorectal neoplasia surveillance. However, administering bowel preparation in this population poses significant challenges for patients, caregivers, and the endoscopy team, including gastroenterologists and nurses. Despite these challenges, there is limited peer-reviewed guidance on optimal bowel preparation strategies for these patients. This review summarizes the current data on bowel preparation in patients with surgically altered anatomy, identifies key challenges, addresses existing gaps in knowledge, and presents a tailored approach to bowel preparation in this population based on institutional protocol. In addition, we propose future directions for research and quality improvement to enhance outcomes in this cohort.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The National Accreditation Program for Rectal Cancer, developed by the American College of Surgeons Commission on Cancer, was established to standardize and improve the quality of rectal cancer care. While prior research has focused primarily on clinical outcomes, limited evidence exists on how National Accreditation Program for Rectal Cancer accreditation affects patient volume and geographical reach in a community hospital setting. This project evaluates the impact of National Accreditation Program for Rectal Cancer accreditation on rectal cancer patient volume and the geographic distribution of patients seeking care. Retrospective observational study conducted from July 2016 through December 2024 at a single community-based hospital. Monthly and annual rectal cancer patient volumes and patient zip codes were collected and analyzed to determine changes over time. The average monthly rectal cancer patient volume increased from 1.0 patient per month preaccreditation to 4.58 patients per month postaccreditation. However, the segmented Poisson regression did not yield a statistically significant change across all periods. The geographic catchment area expanded from 22 zip codes to 79 zip codes after accreditation. Average patient distance traveled increased by 6 miles, but the change did not reach statistical significance. National Accreditation Program for Rectal Cancer accreditation was associated with an increase in patient volume and a broader geographic scope of patients seeking care at a community hospital; however, this change cannot be disentangled from the hiring of 2 fellowship-trained colorectal surgeons. Accreditation may serve as a signal to patients and referring providers of high-quality, disease-specific care, potentially enhancing the institution's competitive standing and patient draw in the health care marketplace.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Postoperative recovery of body composition in patients with gastric cancer (GC) and colorectal cancer (CRC) is a complex and dynamic process. However, longitudinal recovery patterns across multiple physiological domains remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to describe longitudinal changes in body composition over 12 months after curative surgery in patients with GC and CRC. This prospective longitudinal study evaluated serial changes in body composition parameters, including body weight, skeletal muscle index (SMI), phase angle (PhA), and the extracellular water to total body water ratio (ECW/TBW), from the preoperative period to 12 months after curative surgery in 138 patients, comprising 61 patients with GC and 77 patients with CRC. Distinct and time-dependent recovery patterns were observed across body composition domains. Body weight and SMI gradually declined after surgery, reaching their lowest levels at approximately 3 months postoperatively, followed by partial recovery at 6 and 12 months; however, complete restoration to preoperative values was not achieved in several subgroups. In contrast, PhA declined abruptly on postoperative day 1, while ECW/TBW peaked at the same time point, representing the most prominent early postoperative changes in these parameters. Descriptive subgroup patterns suggested less complete recovery of SMI, PhA, and ECW/TBW among elderly, low skeletal muscle mass, advanced-stage, and chemotherapy-treated patients. Patients with low skeletal muscle mass showed persistently lower SMI values, whereas advanced-stage and chemotherapy-treated patients appeared to show slower normalization of PhA and ECW/TBW. Postoperative changes in body composition appeared to occur asynchronously across multiple physiological domains in patients with gastric and colorectal cancer. Several clinically vulnerable subgroups, including older patients, patients with low skeletal muscle mass or advanced-stage disease, and patients who received chemotherapy, showed descriptive patterns suggestive of less complete recovery. Serial body composition assessment over an extended follow-up period may help characterize postoperative changes and provide a basis for future hypothesis-driven studies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early detection of colorectal cancer is of paramount importance. Polyp segmentation using deep learning models can play an important role in this process; however, these models require large annotated datasets that are difficult to obtain in medical imaging. In this work, we propose FCVGAN (Fuzzy C-Means Conditional Variational Autoencoder Generative Adversarial Network), a mask-conditional generative framework that combines Fuzzy C-Means clustering, a Conditional VAE, and a SPADE-based GAN with a multi-scale discriminator. We evaluate two augmentation strategies across four polyp datasets: per-dataset training and transfer learning from Kvasir-SEG. The segmentation experiments repeated across five independent seeds show that transfer augmentation is the strategy that achieved the highest mean Dice score on three of the four datasets, while per-dataset augmentation performed best on Kvasir-Sessile. Compared with the corresponding baselines, transfer augmentation improved the mean Dice score by 2.4%, 0.8%, 16.0%, and 6.2% on Kvasir-SEG, CVC-ClinicDB, Kvasir-Sessile, and ETIS-Larib, respectively. The statistical analysis also showed large effect sizes for transfer augmentation over the baseline across all datasets. When performing the generation quality analysis, per-dataset training achieved a better average FID. However, the images generated with transfer learning showed lower similarity to the training data, which suggests that visual fidelity alone is not a complete indicator of augmentation effectiveness. The ablation study across the five configurations also showed that the contribution of the FCVGAN components depends on the dataset, with the full FCVGAN model providing the most balanced performance across the evaluated datasets. Overall, FCVGAN provides an effective framework for synthetic polyp augmentation, while transfer learning offers a practical strategy for supporting multiple target datasets using a single trained generator.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common malignancies worldwide, and the prognosis of patients with metastatic disease remains poor. Solute carrier proteins participate in diverse cellular processes, yet the biological and clinical relevance of the SLC35D family in CRC remains largely unexplored. This study systematically investigated the expression patterns and clinical significance of SLC35D family members and further evaluated the functional role of SLC35D1 in CRC. Bioinformatic analyses using TCGA and other publicly available datasets and analytical platforms were performed to evaluate the expression patterns and clinical significance of SLC35D family members in CRC. Associations of SLC35D1 expression with patient survival, immune cell infiltration, immune checkpoint markers, and cancer-related transcriptional programs were examined. Loss- and gain-of-function experiments in CRC cells were performed to assess the effects of SLC35D1 on cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT-related phenotypes. SLC35D1 expression was significantly decreased in CRC tissues, SLC35D2 showed a nonsignificant downward trend, and SLC35D3 was significantly increased. Lower SLC35D1 expression was associated with poorer clinical outcomes in the TCGA cohort, although this prognostic association was not reproduced in the independent GSE39582 cohort. Bioinformatic analyses further revealed associations between SLC35D1 expression and immune cell infiltration, immune checkpoint markers, and several cancer-related transcriptional programs. Although the association between SLC35D1 and the EMT-related signature was modest, pathway-enrichment analyses suggested a potential relationship with EMT-related processes. Consistent with these observations, loss- and gain-of-function studies showed that SLC35D1 expression was associated with changes in CRC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT-related molecular phenotypes. Our findings identify SLC35D1 as an understudied SLC35D family member associated with CRC progression and clinical outcome. Functional studies showed that modulation of SLC35D1 expression was associated with changes in malignant phenotypes in CRC cells, whereas its relationships with EMT-related programs and the tumor immune microenvironment warrant further mechanistic investigation. These findings suggest that SLC35D1 may have prognostic relevance in CRC, although its prognostic value requires further validation in independent clinical cohorts.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Capsaicin, the principal bioactive compound of chilli peppers, has emerged as a promising natural molecule with anticancer potential in several malignancies, including colorectal cancer. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its effects in colorectal cancer cells remain incompletely understood. In the present study, we investigated the effects of capsaicin on Caco-2 human colorectal adenocarcinoma cells, focusing on cell viability, proliferation, migration, cell-cycle regulation, and autophagy. Capsaicin (50-200 µM) reduced cell viability in a dose- and time-dependent manner and significantly inhibited proliferation and migratory capacity. Capsaicin induced G2/M cell-cycle arrest, accompanied by increased p21 expression and reduced p53 phosphorylation. Notably, capsaicin-induced cytotoxicity was not associated with activation of caspase-dependent apoptosis and was instead associated with marked accumulation of autophagic structures and increased LC3B-II/LAMP-1 co-localization. Chloroquine co-treatment failed to further increase LC3B-II or p62 accumulation, indicating that autophagic degradation was already impaired. Although lysosomal abundance remained unchanged, capsaicin significantly reduced mature cathepsin-D protein, demonstrating compromised lysosomal degradative capacity and defective autophagic flux. In addition, capsaicin upregulated occludin expression, suggesting enhanced tight-junction integrity and reduced migratory potential. Collectively, these findings, at least explorative, demonstrate that capsaicin reduces Caco-2 cell viability and induces G2/M cell-cycle arrest, accompanied by p21 upregulation and impaired lysosomal degradative capacity, highlighting disruption of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway as a potential mechanism underlying its anticancer activity in Caco-2 cells.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide. Chronic inflammation plays a pivotal role in CRC development and progression, with cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and interleukin-8 (IL-8) representing key mediators of tumor-promoting inflammation. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of thymoquinone (TQ), 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), and their combination on the expression of COX-2, IL-6, and IL-8 at both the mRNA and protein levels in colorectal cancer cell lines (SW1116 and RKO) and normal colon epithelial cells (CCD-841CoN). Although numerical changes in inflammation-associated mediator expression were observed following TQ monotherapy, none of the TQ-monotherapy comparisons versus the untreated control reached statistical significance after correction for multiple comparisons. Notably, combined TQ/5-FU treatment significantly reduced COX-2 protein levels in SW1116 cells compared with the untreated control. Differences between transcript and protein responses were observed across the investigated cell lines and treatment conditions. However, since both endpoints were assessed at a single time point, the mechanisms underlying these differences cannot be conclusively determined from the present data. Exploratory molecular docking analysis was additionally performed to examine potential direct interactions of TQ with COX-2, IL-6, and IL-8. The predicted docking scores ranged from -5.1 to -6.6 kcal/mol, with the most favorable predicted interaction observed for COX-2. These computational findings are hypothesis-generating and should be interpreted independently of the experimentally observed changes in target expression. Collectively, the present findings demonstrate treatment- and cell-line-dependent response patterns in inflammation-associated mediators, while providing no statistically significant evidence of an effect of TQ monotherapy versus the untreated control under the present experimental conditions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is traditionally viewed as the result of the sequential accumulation of molecular alterations and the clonal expansion of transformed cells. However, the state of morphologically non-neoplastic mucosa preceding the development of neoplasia remains considerably less well characterized. This narrative review aims to integrate evidence on biliary and lipid metabolism, intestinal transit, microbial metabolism, and field cancerization and to formulate a testable model of early metabolic remodeling in the distal colon. We propose that a chronically altered biliary-metabolic environment, combined with prolonged luminal and mucosa-associated exposure, may promote lipid-metabolic remodeling of morphologically non-neoplastic mucosa. This state is considered not as a new disease entity but as a potential tissue phenotype capable of altering the barrier, metabolic, and regenerative properties of the epithelium. Subsequent exposure to nitrogen-containing products of microbial metabolism may sustain repeated cycles of injury and regeneration, thereby creating conditions for clonal selection. Following the emergence of a neoplastic clone, the same local environment may potentially assume a different biological role and become part of a metabolic niche that supports further clonal expansion. The proposed model extends the concept of field cancerization by incorporating a metabolic dimension and generates a series of spatial and temporal predictions amenable to experimental and prospective clinical testing. Validation of this model may provide a basis for investigating morphologically non-neoplastic mucosa as potential tissue at risk and for developing earlier preventive and diagnostic approaches.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer remains a serious public health challenge in the United States. Six major cancers (female breast, colorectal, liver, lung/bronchus, pancreas, and prostate) account for a substantial proportion of the national cancer burden. Understanding the changes in the incidence of these cancers over time can provide insights for prevention and control. This study examined temporal trends in the cancer incidence according to age at onset and stage at diagnosis. This population-based study analyzed data from the United States Cancer Statistics database for 2001-2023, including all 50 states and the District of Columbia. Joinpoint regression was used to estimate annual percent changes (APCs) and average annual percent changes (AAPCs), with corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs), based on age-adjusted incidence rates per 100,000 people. Of note, incidence rates from 2020 data were excluded from the Joinpoint models because COVID-19 pandemic disruptions affected cancer screening, diagnosis, and reporting. From 2001 to 2023, the incidence of lung and colorectal cancers declined, particularly among older adults (aged ≥50 years) (lung cancer: AAPC -2.09; 95% CI: -2.27, -1.90; colorectal cancer AAPC -2.70; 95% CI: -2.83, -2.56). In contrast, the incidence of colorectal, pancreatic, and breast cancers increased among younger adults (aged <50 years), whereas the incidence of liver and lung cancer declined. Moreover, prostate cancer incidence declined over time despite modest rebound in recent years (AAPC 1.83; 95% CI: 0.53, 3.14). Stage-specific analyses revealed increasing rates of early-stage diagnoses for several cancers, while late-stage cancer incidence increased for pancreatic and colorectal cancers (especially among younger adults). Cancer incidence varied substantially by cancer type, age, and stage at diagnosis. The rising incidence of colorectal, pancreatic, and breast cancers among younger adults underscores the need for continued research into risk factors, early detection, and prevention strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Given the important role of early detection in improving cancer outcomes, epigenetic alterations, particularly DNA methylation, have emerged as powerful biomarkers for cancer screening and diagnosis. However, methylation profiling of cfDNA (circulating free DNA) presents particular technical challenges because cfDNA is typically present at very low concentrations and is highly fragmented. Bisulfite conversion, although essential for distinguishing methylated from unmethylated cytosines, can further compromise DNA integrity through chemical-induced loss of DNA during purification steps. Inadequate conversion or excessive DNA loss may consequently reduce library complexity, increase DNA duplication rates, and negatively affect mapping efficiency and downstream sequencing quality. Therefore, optimizing bisulfite conversion is particularly important for reliable methylation profiling of low-input cfDNA. The effectiveness of these diagnostic approaches relies on the accurate detection of DNA methylation patterns, which is fundamentally dependent on the efficiency of bisulfite conversion of genomic DNA. This pilot study aims to compare the performance of two widely used bisulfite conversion kits, namely the EpiTect Bisulfite (EpiTect) Kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany) and the EZ DNA Methylation (Zymo) Kit (Zymo Research, Irvine, CA, USA), in the context of plasma-derived cfDNA methylation profiling using five samples, including two plasma samples from metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) patients collected at the Department of Gastrointestinal Oncology at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, in Houston, TX, USA, and two plasma samples from healthy donors (controls) purchased from Innovative Research (Novi, MI, USA), along with one control DNA sample (Corriel NA12878-N88). Our objective was to evaluate and compare their conversion efficiency, mapping efficiency (percentage of mapped and unmapped reads), duplication rate, and distribution of methylated cytosines in CpG, CHG, and CHH contexts. Our results indicate that samples processed using the Zymo kit consistently outperformed those treated with the EpiTect kit across multiple performance metrics. The Zymo-treated samples yielded a higher concentration of cfDNA following bisulfite conversion (125.34 nM vs. 45.60 nM in samples processed with the Epitect kit). Additionally, the Zymo kit achieved a higher average bisulfite conversion efficiency (99.3% vs. 95.7%), as well as a significantly higher average mapping rate (94.86% vs. 72.4%), with fewer unmapped reads and lower duplication rates. Head-to-head comparison of Bismark methylation calls across the same reference regions showed high concordance between the two protocols. The SEPT9 region was strongly hypermethylated with both protocols (100% with EpiTect and approximately 94% with Zymo), whereas the BMP3 region was predominantly unmethylated (approximately 4% with EpiTect and 7% with Zymo). These findings suggest that the Zymo kit demonstrated improved performance under the conditions evaluated for cfDNA methylation analysis compared to the EpiTect protocol. Further investigation using a larger number of samples is needed to validate our findings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastric cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related death, and its malignant behavior is driven in large part by dysregulated post-translational modifications (PTMs). Yet the prevailing tendency to study individual modifications in isolation has obscured a defining feature of PTM biology: modifications frequently interact, competing for the same residue or cooperating across residues to form regulatory switches that dictate protein fate. This review synthesizes the PTM crosstalk framework in gastric cancer around three principal axes-phosphorylation-ubiquitination relays, SUMOylation-ubiquitination interplay, and metabolic coupling through lactylation-and traces how these axes translate into the hallmarks of proliferation, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and immune evasion. The framework is further extended to colorectal cancer to separate shared regulatory principles from cancer-specific switches. Central to this account is the proposition that oncogenic output is governed not by any single modification but by the balance among competing and cooperating marks, and that the switch enzymes maintaining this balance constitute the most informative therapeutic targets. Translating this view into therapy will require selective degraders and inhibitors, crosstalk-aware biomarkers, and systematic multi-omics maps of the modification network.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Minimally invasive surgical (MIS) techniques have fundamentally transformed the management of colorectal cancer. Since the early 1990s, the field has rapidly evolved, shifting from initial concerns about oncologic safety to the widespread adoption of both laparoscopic and robotic surgeries. Specifically, laparoscopic approaches to colorectal cancer resection are now widely adopted and supported by robust randomized controlled trial evidence demonstrating favorable perioperative outcomes with equivalent oncologic results compared to open surgery. Robotic-assisted platforms have gained increasing adoption; however, their incremental clinical and oncologic benefit over laparoscopy remains under active investigation. As these technologies have been implemented, significant challenges related to surgical proficiency and economic sustainability have emerged. MIS approaches, particularly laparoscopic colectomies and proctectomies, involve steep, multidimensional learning curves that require substantial case volumes to achieve technical mastery and consistent clinical outcomes. Simultaneously, the rising costs of robotic platforms raise important considerations regarding the financial sustainability of healthcare systems. While robotic surgery may reduce certain downstream costs through shorter hospital stays and fewer complications, its substantially higher upfront operative costs and uncertain cost-effectiveness relative to laparoscopy require careful consideration, and access remains a barrier, particularly for patients without private insurance. This narrative review describes the evolution of MIS in colorectal cancer treatment and examines the dual considerations of the surgical learning curve and hospital cost implications.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is biologically heterogeneous, resulting in variable outcomes despite similar disease burden and treatment. Although metastasectomy offers the only potentially curative option for selected patients, surgical selection remains largely anatomy based. Whether biological factors continue to influence outcomes after resection remains unclear. We retrospectively analysed 290 consecutive patients with stage IV colorectal adenocarcinoma treated at a Brazilian tertiary oncology centre (2003-2019). Tumour sidedness, RAS mutational status, and metastasectomy were evaluated for overall survival (OS) using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression in the overall cohort and the metastasectomy subgroup. Median OS was 40.2 months. Patients undergoing metastasectomy had significantly longer survival than those managed non-operatively (median 116.0 vs. 30.1 months; 5-year OS 63% vs. 14%; Tumour biology remains a dominant determinant of survival in mCRC even after metastasectomy. These data challenge purely anatomy-based surgical paradigms and support integrating molecular and clinicopathological risk into post-resection management and treatment planning.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The effectiveness of chemotherapy in colorectal cancer (CRC) is significantly reduced by acquired chemoresistance to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), oxaliplatin and irinotecan. This structured narrative review synthesises mechanistic, preclinical, translational and clinical evidence underlying resistance to these agents. Distinct drug-specific molecular mechanisms can underlie acquired chemoresistance, whereas shared adaptive survival processes support treatment persistence and may, in some settings, contribute to the emergence of stable acquired resistance. 5-FU resistance is associated with factors such as altered thymidylate synthase activity, drug catabolism, nucleotide metabolism and apoptosis avoidance, whereas resistance to oxaliplatin involves enhanced deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) repair, detoxification, reduced platinum accumulation and metabolic adaptation. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Palliative chemotherapy for unresectable colorectal liver metastases (uCRLM) yields poor long-term survival. Liver transplantation (LT) is an emerging curative option for highly selected patients with liver-only disease. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA guidelines. Electronic databases were searched for studies evaluating LT for uCRLM. Overall survival (OS) from comparative studies was pooled using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2 and ROBINS-I V2. Potential patient overlap between cohorts from the same transplant programs was assessed and, where present, only 1 report per cohort contributed to pooling. Seventeen studies were included, with 3 comparative studies providing data for meta-analysis. Pooled analysis favored LT over best alternative therapies (HR 0.45, 95% CI 0.28-0.72; P = .0009; I² = 3%). This estimate was not robust: the TransMet randomized trial contributed 63% of the pooled weight, and its exclusion rendered the effect nonsignificant (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.30-1.35). Comparators were clinically heterogeneous, spanning chemotherapy alone, mixed best alternative therapy, and ALPPS, so the pooled hazard ratio should not be read as a single transferable estimate of transplant benefit. Narrative synthesis indicated 5-year OS rates reached 83% following strict biological selection. Post-transplant recurrence was frequent (72%-81.5%) but often amenable to curative-intent management. Referral data, available only from a conference abstract, suggest that approximately 10% of evaluated patients ultimately undergo LT. In highly selected patients with permanently unresectable, liver-confined CRLM, LT is associated with a survival advantage, although the pooled estimate rests principally on a single randomized trial and should not be generalized across the clinically distinct comparators from which it was derived. The benefit appears to be driven by identifying a ``biological elite'' through stringent selection and aggressive multidisciplinary management of recurrences. PROSPERO registration: CRD42025124542.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
There is currently a lack of low-cost, nonintrusive methods for colorectal adenocarcinoma (CRA) detection. Moreover, the application of Raman spectroscopy (RS)-based CRA detection is limited due to its high noise levels and low characterization abilities. Propose a method for the early screening of CRA based on RS and deep learning techniques. An MS-Former (multiscale transformer) method was constructed by combining multiscale convolution and self-attention mechanisms to adapt spectral scenarios based on RS and surface-enhanced Raman spectra (SERS) at the cellular and patient serum levels, respectively. Furthermore, Raman spectral critical frequency test (classifying the spectrum extracted from each threshold by linear discriminant analysis (LDA) using the classical machine learning method) was performed and the concerning Raman shifts were screened in the identification process of different samples. At the cellular level, the proposed model can identify normal cells and cancer cells at an accuracy of 99.12%. At the serum level, for the first time, this model achieved AUC values of 98.45% and 99.40% in identification of adenoma and adenocarcinoma, respectively. When classifying patients into groups of healthy, adenoma, and adenocarcinoma, the single Raman detection and individual level accuracy were 94.78%, 100%, respectively. Matching metabolites were obtained through matching the screened Raman shifts, which greatly improved the interpretability and biological significance of the results. The proposed model can conveniently and rapidly screens patients with colorectal adenomas and adenocarcinomas, requiring no pretreatment and exhibiting extremely high accuracy and low cost.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the most common form of lung cancer and is often diagnosed at an advanced stage, leading to poor prognosis. Carcinoembryonic antigen-related cell adhesion molecule 5 (CEACAM5) has emerged as a potential biomarker in colorectal and other gastrointestinal cancer; however, its role in NSCLC remains unexplored. This study evaluated the prognostic role of the CEACAM5 biomarker in metastatic non-squamous (mNSQ) NSCLC using real-world data. CEACAM5 expression was assessed via immunohistochemistry of archival tissue from 336 eligible patients. Real-world overall survival (rwOS) was the primary outcome analyzed across six treatment cohorts. Secondary outcomes included prevalence of CEACAM5 expression (high, moderate, negative) by cohort and tumor site (primary vs. metastatic) and other outcomes including real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS), time to next treatment (rwTTNT), and time to treatment discontinuation (rwTTD). High CEACAM5 expression was observed in approximately 18% of the overall population, with consistent levels observed across both primary and metastatic tumor samples. No significant associations were found between different CEACAM5 expression levels and rwOS, rwPFS, rwTTNT, and rwTTD, across all cohorts. CEACAM5 did not demonstrate prognostic value in this retrospective cohort study of patients with metastatic NSCLC. Further research to confirm our findings is needed.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Synchronous bilateral renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is an uncommon clinical presentation that raises important diagnostic, surgical, and oncological management challenges. Colonic serosal metastases from RCC represent a particularly rare site of spread. We report the case of a 67-year-old man with synchronous bilateral clear cell RCC (ccRCC) who underwent staged nephrectomies in 2022, followed by early multifocal recurrence necessitating completion left nephrectomy, bilateral adrenalectomy, and segmental colectomy for serosal colonic involvement in October 2023. Pathology confirmed metastatic ccRCC at all resected sites. Adjuvant pembrolizumab was initiated post-resection but failed to prevent rapid systemic progression with bone and pulmonary metastases. Following adjuvant immunotherapy failure, the patient received three sequential lines of targeted therapy in the metastatic setting: sunitinib (first line), everolimus (second line), and cabozantinib (third line). Cabozantinib achieved a durable metabolic response, with complete resolution of nodal disease and partial response of bone and pulmonary lesions, despite prior multiline exposure. Treatment was complicated by medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw, requiring temporary discontinuation; cabozantinib was reintroduced at a reduced dose (20 mg/day), which was associated with maintained disease control and acceptable tolerance. At the time of reporting, the patient remained on reduced-dose cabozantinib with chronic hemodialysis and hormonal replacement, maintaining an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0. This case illustrates the biological heterogeneity and unusual metastatic tropism of ccRCC, and underscores the clinical value of individualized multidisciplinary management; combining aggressive metastasectomy, palliative radiotherapy, and sequential targeted systemic therapy, in achieving meaningful long-term disease control while preserving quality of life.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The tumour microenvironment comprises a variety of cell types that interact with malignant cells, influencing both cancer progression and the patient response to therapy. Given the intricate interactions among these components, assessing how signalling pathways contribute to cancer progression by acting on different components of the TME is particularly complex. Multiplexed imaging allows simultaneous assessment of signalling in multiple of these components. Here, we utilise a highly multiplexed dataset of 61 markers across 746 colorectal tumours to investigate how complex mTOR signalling in different tissue compartments influences patient prognosis. We found that mTOR pathway signalling in immune cells correlates with favourable patient survival. Advanced spatially-aware analysis of signalling activities using graph neural networks revealed that the positive association between immune mTOR signalling and patient survival was more pronounced in tumours with features of a more differentiated morphology. Integrative analysis using TCGA data and spatial transcriptomics confirmed a role for immune mTOR signalling in immune activation, accompanied by reduced TGF-β signalling. Our work highlights the importance of adopting a personalised approach to targeting mTOR in cancer patients and establishes a framework for studying cell type-specific signalling in the TME.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Microsatellite stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC), accounting for over 85% of advanced cases, shows intrinsic resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors due to an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. The renin-angiotensin system (RAS), particularly angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R), has been implicated in tumor progression and immune evasion. This study investigated whether telmisartan, a selective AT1R antagonist, modulates programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression and enhances anti-tumor immunity in MSS CRC. Mismatch repair (MMR) protein expression was characterized in human (SW480, HT29, HCT116) and murine (CT26) CRC cell lines. The effects of telmisartan on cell viability, PD-L1 expression, STAT3 signaling, and migration were evaluated using Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8), Western blotting, and Transwell assays. A CT26 tumor model in BALB/c mice was used to assess therapeutic efficacy alone or combined with pembrolizumab, with immunohistochemical analysis of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes. Public transcriptomic analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) CRC data and immune infiltration analysis using the CIBERSORT (Cell-type Identification By Estimating Relative Subsets Of RNA Transcripts) algorithm were further performed. Telmisartan (10-20 μM) reduced PD-L1 expression in both MSS and MSI-H CRC cell lines without significant cytotoxicity. It was associated with increased signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) phosphorylation and reduced cell migration. Telmisartan may remodel the tumor immune microenvironment, potentially through modulation of PD-L1 expression associated with STAT3 signaling, thereby enhancing the response of MSS CRC to immune checkpoint blockade. These findings suggest that telmisartan could serve as a potential immunotherapy adjuvant for MSS CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In China, colorectal cancer (CLC) is the third most common malignancy, following lung cancer and thyroid cancer. This study attempts to reveal the protective mechanism of ubiquitin-specific peptidase 11 (USP11) on Warburg effect of CLC. The study used single-cell analysis and the Chinese Glioma Genome Atlas (CGGA) dataset. HCT-116 cells were transfected with the USP11 or small interfering (si)-USP11 plasmid, respectively. The USP11 messengerRNA(mRNA) expression in patients with CLC was elevated compared to the normal group. Patients with high USP11 expression exhibited poorer survival than those with low USP11 expression in CLC. USP11 was expressed in the epithelial cells of CLC patients. USP11 promoted Warburg effect to induce cell growth progression of CLC. USP11 upregulates the expression of HIF-1α and YAP in CLC. Mechanistically, HIF-1α mediates the effect of USP11 in CLC by driving the progression of the Warburg effect. USP11 physically interacts with the HIF-1α complex and stabilizes HIF-1α protein in CLC cells via suppressing HIF-1α ubiquitination. Additionally, the N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methyltransferase METTL3 enhances USP11 stability in a YTHDF1-dependent manner. This study demonstrates that the METTL3-mediated m6A modification facilitates USP11 stabilization by YTHDF1 in CLC models, providing novel mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic targets for the clinical management of CLC and other malignant tumors.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) is increasing globally, yet prognostic tools specifically tailored to younger patients remain limited. Molecular markers such as mismatch repair (MMR) status, although biologically important, are not routinely available in many clinical settings, creating a translational gap between laboratory advances and bedside practice. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a practical nomogram for predicting overall survival (OS) in EOCRC using widely accessible clinicopathological variables and routine hematological biomarkers, thereby bridging routine laboratory data to individualized risk stratification. This retrospective study included 410 EOCRC patients who underwent radical surgery (training cohort n=246, internal validation n=164). An independent external cohort (n=91) from a second tertiary center was used for validation. Candidate predictors included T/N stage, presenting symptoms, tumor markers [carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9)], and the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII)-a composite biomarker reflecting the balance between tumor-promoting inflammation and antitumor immunity. A nomogram was constructed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and multivariable Cox regression. Model performance was assessed by discrimination [time-dependent area under the curve (AUC)], calibration, decision curve analysis (DCA), risk stratification, and head-to-head comparison with an anatomical-stage model and a clinicopathological model without inflammatory biomarkers. Six predictors were retained in the final nomogram: T stage, N stage, changes in bowel habits, CEA, CA19-9, and SII. For 3-year OS, the AUC was 0.897 (training), 0.837 (internal validation), and 0.861 (external validation); for 5-year OS, the corresponding AUCs were 0.904, 0.873, and 0.868. The nomogram significantly outperformed the anatomical-stage model in all cohorts (all P<0.001) and provided incremental value over the clinicopathological model in both validation cohorts. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed survival probabilities. DCA confirmed clinical net benefit across a range of threshold probabilities. The nomogram successfully stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups (log-rank P<0.001 in all three cohorts). This externally validated nomogram translates routinely available clinicopathological and hematological data into individualized OS predictions for EOCRC. By integrating inflammatory biomarkers such as SII, the model provides a translatable tool that may support risk-stratified surveillance and management, particularly in clinical settings where routine hematological and clinicopathological assessments are available but comprehensive molecular profiling is not.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Surgery is central to the management of localized colorectal cancer (CRC), whereas surgical decision-making in metastatic disease is more complex and highly individualized. This study aimed to investigate patterns of primary-site surgery recorded in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, reasons for no surgery, patient and tumor characteristics, and observed overall survival (OS) in non-metastatic CRC, with a separate exploratory analysis of surgical patterns in metastatic disease. CRC tumor records diagnosed between 2006 and 2015 were identified according to prespecified eligibility criteria. Non-metastatic (M0) disease was the primary cohort. Descriptive analyses characterized recorded surgery, reasons for no surgery, baseline features, and survival; multivariable Cox regression, propensity-score matching (PSM), and sensitivity analyses estimated adjusted associations. Metastatic (M1) disease was analyzed separately as an exploratory cohort. Among 14,130 M0 tumor records, five with unknown surgery status were excluded, leaving 13,807 with and 318 without recorded primary-site surgery. Surgery was not recommended in 213 of 318 no-surgery records (67.0%), and the method used to determine regional nodal status differed markedly by surgery status [absolute standardized mean difference (SMD), 2.158]. Median OS was 164 months with recorded surgery and 59 months without recorded surgery (log-rank P<0.001). In the primary Cox model, recorded surgery was associated with a lower average hazard of death over follow-up [hazard ratio (HR), 0.457; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.397-0.527; P<0.001], but the proportional hazards assumption was not met. PSM yielded 317 pairs; the pair-stratified HR was 0.453 (95% CI: 0.344-0.598; P<0.001), and 60-month OS was 74.1% versus 50.2%. The M1 cohort comprised 694 tumor records. In the 2010-2015 subset (n=467), records without primary-site surgery more often had lung metastasis, bone metastasis, and at least two documented organ sites; four recorded surgical patterns were observed. In M0 disease, no recorded primary-site surgery was uncommon, usually reflected that surgery was not recommended, and was associated with substantially shorter observed survival. This association does not quantify the causal effect of surgery. Heterogeneous metastatic distributions and procedure patterns in M1 disease underscore the need for individualized clinical decision-making rather than routine primary-site surgery based on registry survival comparisons.

Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common malignant tumors worldwide, often presenting without apparent early symptoms, and most patients are diagnosed at an advanced stage with a poor prognosis. F-box protein 17 (FBXO17) is up-regulated in various tumors and may represent a potential prognostic marker in CRC. This study sought to elucidate FBXO17's specific role in CRC and the underlying mechanism. FBXO17-silenced and FBXO17-overexpressing CRC cells were established using a lentiviral system and liposome transfection technology, respectively. Cell counting kit-8, Transwell, and wound healing assays, as well as Western blot, were used to assess CRC cell proliferation, invasion, and migration, and to examine Wnt/β-catenin pathway activation. Intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), Fe Compared with human normal colon cells, human CRC cells exhibited generally high FBXO17 expression. Silencing FBXO17 led to decreased CRC cell proliferation, invasion, and migration, attenuated Wnt/β-catenin pathway activation, and enhanced ferroptosis, whereas overexpression of FBXO17 reversed these effects by enhancing CRC cell proliferation, invasion, and migration, activating the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, and suppressing ferroptosis. Furthermore, treatment with ferrostatin-1 (ferroptosis inhibitor) or CHIR-99021 (Wnt/β-catenin pathway agonist) enhanced the proliferation, invasion, and migration of FBXO17-silenced CRC cells while attenuating ferroptosis. Silencing FBXO17 can promote CRC cell ferroptosis but inhibit proliferation, invasion, and migration through suppression of Wnt/β-catenin pathway activation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
There are two main margins in histopathological assessment of colorectal resections for primary adenocarcinoma: non-peritonealised and longitudinal margins (proximal and distal). The Royal College of Pathologists of Australasia (RCPA) recommends microscopic examination of longitudinal margins only if tumour extends within 30 mm macroscopically, unless aggressive features are present. We evaluated the utility of microscopic longitudinal margin assessment by auditing colorectal resections presented at the Royal Prince Alfred Hospital (RPAH) multidisciplinary meetings (between July 2023 and June 2025) and surveying Australasian Gastrointestinal Pathology Society (AGPS) members on sampling practices. A total of 308 specimens were identified, of which all underwent routine longitudinal margin sampling. Findings were present in 2.27% (n=7) of margin sections, including five neoplastic and two non-neoplastic abnormalities. Neoplastic findings included adenocarcinoma (n=2), sessile serrated lesion (n=1), low-grade dysplasia (n=1), and Paget disease (n=1). Both adenocarcinomas were macroscopically identified and margin status was not altered by microscopy. Regarding the survey, there were 82 participants; 89% reported routine universal longitudinal margin sampling and 91% donut sampling. Most participants believed routine microscopic examination of margins rarely yields diagnostic information (91% for longitudinal margins; 68% for donuts). A targeted approach to selective sampling could reduce costs, workload, and environmental impact without compromising patient care.

Examine the impact of injury mechanism and management strategies on outcomes after traumatic rectal injury (TRI). TRI are uncommon, with most data derived from penetrating injuries. Whether management and outcomes differ between blunt (BR) and penetrating (PR) injuries remains unclear. A multicenter study across 22 trauma centers compared management patterns, use of the "4 Ds" adjuncts (drain, diversion, distal washout, direct repair), and outcomes between BR and PR. Among 725 patients (511 PR, 214 BR), BR had higher injury severity, more abdominal complications, and required more interventions despite similar TRI grade. Mortality was lowest in PR managed with adjuncts and highest in BR without adjuncts. In BR, diversion-only management resulted in the highest complication and reintervention rates. Drain and distal washout were also associated with increased abdominal complications. Multivariable analysis showed diversion-only management independently increased complications versus primary repair. BR carry greater morbidity than PR and may favor repair strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
After the Stockholm III trial, a trend towards delayed surgery after neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (5 × 5 Gy) for rectal cancer has emerged in Sweden, driven by the lower short-term complication rates and similar oncological outcomes. This study aimed to examine long-term oncological outcomes after neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy, comparing direct versus delayed surgery for rectal cancer in a real-world setting. A registry-based retrospective national cohort study was conducted using prospectively collected data from the Swedish Colorectal Cancer Registry. Patients with rectal cancer receiving neoadjuvant neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy with surgery between 2016 and 2020 were analysed for oncological outcomes (local recurrence, distant metastasis) and overall survival at 3 years, comparing direct surgery, defined as surgery within 7 days after neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy, and delayed surgery, defined as surgery after 28-90 days. The rate of patients who underwent surgery within the delayed time frame of the Stockholm III trial was also recorded. A total of 2080 patients were identified, of whom 1208 (58.1%) underwent direct surgery and 872 had delayed surgery. Of note, only 288 patients underwent resection 28-56 days after neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (within the time frame of the Stockholm III trial). Although the pathological complete response rate was higher in the delayed-surgery group compared with the direct-surgery group (6.5% versus 0.4%), 3-year local recurrence and distant metastasis rates were, respectively, 1.0% (12 patients) and 6.8% (82) in the direct-surgery group, and 3.4% (30) and 11.9% (104) in the delayed-surgery group. The adjusted hazard ratios for local recurrence and distant metastasis comparing delayed surgery with direct surgery were 3.60 (95 per cent confidence interval 1.75 to 7.39) and 2.17 (1.58 to 2.96), respectively, whereas the adjusted hazard ratio for overall survival was 1.37 (1.06 to 1.77), favouring the direct-surgery group. In a real-world setting, the results indicate that few patients in the delayed-surgery group had surgery within the stipulated time frame. Considering this, delayed surgery was associated with a higher risk of local recurrence, distant metastasis, and reduced overall survival.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Bowel cancer is the fifth most common cancer in Australia and the second leading cause of cancer-related death. Although the National Bowel Cancer Screening Program mails test kits to eligible Australians, uptake remains suboptimal, particularly among underserved populations. The Alternative Access Model (AAM) is a primary care-based strategy through which healthcare providers (HCPs) distribute kits directly to eligible patients, enabling practitioner endorsement and patient navigation. This study explored HCPs' perceptions of the acceptability, feasibility, barriers, and enablers of implementing the AAM in general practices serving ethnically and socioeconomically diverse populations. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with primary HCPs in Melbourne, Australia. Nine general practice clinics participated in a two-phase study. Thirty-seven interviews were conducted with general practitioners (n = 13), practice nurses (n = 15), and practice managers (n = 9). Data were analysed using NVivo 15. Most participants (89%) were unfamiliar with the AAM. Once explained, the model was perceived as acceptable because it aligns with primary care's preventive role; however, implementation would be feasible only if barriers such as lack of financial incentives, system integration, and maintenance are addressed and provided. Improving equitable access requires more than making screening kits available. Tailored, culturally responsive, multi-faceted resources that could address perceived low bowel health literacy and cultural beliefs about screening, along with practitioners' endorsement and encouragement, and enhanced patient navigation within primary care are perceived having potential benefits in supporting more equitable bowel cancer screening participation among underserved populations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oral vaccines hold great promise for colorectal cancer (CRC) immunotherapy but are limited by inefficient mucosal delivery and a lack of spatiotemporal control over immune activation. Here we report a spatiotemporally programmed oral nanovaccine that implements a dual-site vaccination strategy through a sequential and causally linked immune cascade, initiating immune priming in Peyer's patches of the small intestine and subsequently amplifying immunity at colorectal tumor sites. The nanovaccine (DPML@OVA-CpG), composed of antigen- and CpG-loaded mesoporous polydopamine nanoparticles stabilized by β-glucan and plant-derived lipids, resists gastrointestinal degradation and targets gut-associated lymphoid tissues. Following oral administration, it induces robust systemic effector and memory T cell responses via small intestinal priming, while a fraction traffics to colorectal tumors. There, near-infrared irradiation triggers immunogenic cell death of tumor cells and, together with locally released CpG, converts tumors into autologous in situ vaccine factories. This spatiotemporally orchestrated strategy achieves potent therapeutic efficacy against liver metastatic CRC, extending survival compared to PD-L1 antibody therapy and traditional single-site oral vaccination.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ultra-low sphincter-preserving surgery (ULSPS) for low rectal cancer often results in persistent bowel and sexual dysfunction alongside significant psychological distress, which may adversely affect recovery and may be associated with longer-term oncologic outcomes. Evidence on integrated psychosocial interventions in this context remains limited. To evaluate whether a structured six-month psychosocial intervention integrating narrative therapy and cognitive behavioral therapy improves psychological and functional recovery after ultra-low sphincter-preserving surgery for low rectal cancer, and to explore its associations with inflammatory markers, postoperative recovery metrics, and exploratory oncologic outcomes. In this single-centre, randomized controlled trial, 172 patients with AJCC stage I-III low rectal cancer undergoing ULSPS were assigned (1:1) to standard ERAS-based care or an integrated six-month psychosocial program combining narrative therapy and Beck cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT). Primary outcomes included depression (BDI-II), anxiety (BAI), bowel function (LARS), and sexual function (IIEF-5, FSFI). Secondary endpoints comprised inflammatory markers, recovery metrics, and exploratory oncologic outcomes, including disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS). Analyses were performed using linear mixed-effects models, Kaplan-Meier methods, and Cox regression with prespecified covariates. The intervention group demonstrated significantly greater reductions in depression and anxiety, with between-group differences exceeding prespecified clinically meaningful change thresholds. Improvements in bowel and sexual function were clinically and statistically significant, accompanied by lower postoperative CRP, IL-6, and TNF-α. Recovery metrics favored the intervention (shorter hospital stay, earlier bowel recovery). In exploratory survival analyses, 2-year disease-free survival was 89.5% versus 74.4% (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.24-0.96), and overall survival was 92.4% versus 79.1% (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.19-0.93). These oncologic findings should be interpreted cautiously because DFS and OS were secondary exploratory outcomes, the number of events was modest, follow-up was relatively short, and the study was conducted at a single centre. An integrated narrative-CBT intervention was associated with clinically meaningful improvements in emotional and functional recovery after ULSPS for low rectal cancer. Favorable DFS and OS estimates were observed as exploratory secondary findings but should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than definitive evidence of oncologic benefit. These findings support further evaluation of structured psychosocial programs as adjuncts to ERAS-based perioperative care pathways.

Early functional reactivity to a CEACAM5 x CD3 T cell bispecific antibody in solid tumors associates with baseline immune contexture rather than target antigen density alone.
NPJ Precision Oncology · 2026-08 · Wilson S, Silva A, Serrano-Serrano ML, Karanikas V, Waldhauer I, Schoenle A, et al.
意义与启示：该研究揭示实体瘤对CEACAM5×CD3 TCB的早期药效取决于基线免疫浸润而非CEA表达，提示肠癌肝转移治疗需结合免疫分型，并支持EVOC平台用于临床前药效评估。

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Clinical translation of T cell bispecific (TCB) therapies in solid tumors is hindered by the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and intratumoral heterogeneity, features poorly captured by standard preclinical models. We applied an integrated translational framework, combining humanized mouse models, a patient-derived ex vivo organ culture (EVOC) platform, and Phase 1 clinical trial data (ClinTrials.gov identifier NCT03539484), to define the biologic determinants of functional reactivity to a CEACAM5 x CD3 TCB. In humanized mice bearing CEA-positive tumors, the TCB inhibited tumor growth and increased intratumoral T cell infiltration. EVOC, which preserves native 3D tumor architecture and endogenous tumor immune contexture, revealed rapid TCB-induced secretion of IFNγ, IL-2, TNFα, and IL-10 across colorectal, pancreatic, and non-small cell lung cancer patient tumors, with substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. Higher baseline CD3+ T cell infiltration trended with a greater magnitude of cytokine release in patient tumors treated with the TCB ex vivo versus tumors with lower CD3+ T cell infiltration. Baseline tumor CEA expression did not associate with functional response in EVOC. In the Phase 1 trial, on-treatment peripheral cytokine induction was greater in patients with immune-inflamed or -excluded tumors as compared to those with immune-desert tumors. EVOC recapitulated the high inter-patient functional heterogeneity observed clinically, with a coefficient of variation for IFNγ of 135% in EVOC versus 190% in patients, compared with 52% in humanized mice. These findings suggest that early pharmacodynamic responses to CEACAM5 x CD3 TCB associate with a pre-existing tumor immune state rather than target antigen expression alone and support integration of patient-derived ex vivo models for modeling clinically-relevant pharmacodynamics.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Indocyanine green is a fluorescent dye used in a wide range of specialties, including colorectal surgery. Although indocyanine green fluorescence imaging has been well established for assessing colorectal anastomotic perfusion, its role in lymph node mapping in colorectal cancer remains unclear. This narrative review aimed to provide an overview of the mechanism of action of indocyanine green-fluorescence imaging and its role in lymph node mapping in colorectal cancer. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched through July 2026 for studies evaluating the use of indocyanine green-fluorescence imaging for lymphatic mapping and lymph node identification in colorectal cancer. Findings were narratively summarized. Indocyanine green-fluorescence imaging may improve visualization of lymphatic drainage and support a more complete lymphadenectomy. Meta-analyses have reported pooled lymph node detection rates of 91% and 86.8%, with substantial variation by tumor location, disease stage, and mapping technique, with generally lower detection rates in rectal than in colon cancer. Pooled sensitivities of 63%, 64.3%, and 71% were reported, corresponding to false-negative rates of 37%, 35.7%, and 29%, respectively. Although indocyanine green-fluorescence imaging was associated with an increased lymph node harvest and occasionally modified resection strategy, data on long-term survival remain limited and inconsistent. Heterogeneity in indocyanine green dose and concentration, injection route and timing, imaging platforms, and outcome definitions limits comparison across studies. Indocyanine green-fluorescence imaging might be a valuable tool for intraoperative lymphatic mapping and enhancing lymphadenectomy; however, substantial methodologic heterogeneity precludes definitive conclusions regarding its diagnostic accuracy for nodal metastatic status. Standardized protocols and high-quality prospective studies are needed to define its optimal role and long-term oncologic impact.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
While substantial evidence supports a protective effect of aspirin against colorectal polyps and cancer, the evidence for non-aspirin non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NA-NSAIDs) remains limited. We studied the association between the use of NA-NSAIDs and the detection of colorectal polyps and cancer among screening participants. We selected participants in the Bowel Cancer Screening trial in Norway-a randomized trial comparing once-only sigmoidoscopy and the biennial faecal immunochemical test (FIT). Using multivariable logistic regression, we estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the association between NA-NSAID use in the 4 years before the screening invitation and detection of colorectal cancer (CRC), adenomas, advanced adenomas, and advanced serrated polyps. Long-term use was defined as ≥2 years of use. Of 64,889 participants (24,159 sigmoidoscopy, 40,730 FIT), 35,867 (55.3%) were NA-NSAID users, 314 (0.5%) had CRC, 6,208 (9.6%) had adenomas, and 659 (1.0%) had advanced serrated polyps. NA-NSAID users had lower odds of CRC (OR 0.80; 95% CI 0.64-1.00), adenomas (OR 0.94; 95% CI 0.89-1.00), and advanced adenomas (OR 0.87; 95% CI 0.80-0.95) than those with no NA-NSAID prescription. For non-selective NA-NSAIDs, the results were similar to those for any NA-NSAIDs (CRC: OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.63-0.99; adenomas: OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.88-0.99; advanced adenomas: OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.79-0.95). COX2-selective NA-NSAIDs were not associated with CRC or adenomas. Among the long-term NA-NSAIDs users, the ORs were 0.59 (95% CI 0.27-1.26) for CRC, 0.65 (95% CI 0.54-0.79) for adenomas, and 0.59 (95% CI 0.44-0.80) for advanced adenomas. No association was observed between any NA-NSAID use and advanced serrated polyps. The results were consistent across trial arms and sexes. Our findings suggest that use of NA-NSAIDs, in particular non-selective NA-NSAIDs, might be associated with a reduced risk of adenomas and CRC, but not advanced serrated polyps.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We present the case of an older adult man with prolonged fever of unknown origin and a persistent rectangular erythematous plaque, highlighting the diagnostic value of careful skin examination in patients with systemic inflammatory symptoms. This 70-year-old man with adult-onset endogenous eczema, hypertension, stage II upper rectal carcinoma following resection and adjuvant radiotherapy and chemotherapy and left hip avascular necrosis presented with fever persisting for 1 month following an upper respiratory tract infection. He developed generalised arthralgia and bilateral lower limb oedema, accompanied by poor oral intake. Initial treatment with amoxicillin- clavulanate and intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam provided temporary relief. Physical examination revealed generalised xerosis, with an incidental finding of an erythematous, non-tender, mildly indurated, rectangular patch measuring 10x20 cm at the lower back, unnoticeable by the patient. Bilateral inguinal lymph nodes measuring 2x1 cm were palpable. Bilateral pedal oedema with joint bogginess was also present. Laboratory investigations showed leucocytosis with neutrophilia without blasts, normochromic normocytic anaemia, hypoalbuminaemia, transaminitis and elevated inflammatory markers. Imaging (computed tomography and positron emission tomography scans) revealed mild left pleural effusion with multiple subcentimetre lymphadenopathies above and below the diaphragm. Tuberculosis, malignancy and autoimmune markers were negative. Skin biopsy showed scattered single dyskeratotic cells at the upper epidermis, with mild-to-moderate mixed perivascular inflammation including lymphocytes, neutrophils and eosinophils at the upper dermis. Atypical cutaneous manifestations may serve as a valuable clue to adult-onset Still's disease; however, the diagnosis should be established only after careful exclusion of infectious, malignant and autoimmune mimics.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In colorectal cancer, the AJCC T category is defined by the depth of bowel wall invasion rather than by the absolute size of the primary tumor. The clinical value of tumor size in assessing tumor aggressiveness, metastatic risk, and prognosis remains insufficiently investigated. To evaluate the clinical value of tumor size in assessing potential metastatic risk and prognostic stratification in colorectal cancer. We retrospectively included 10,513 patients with colorectal cancer who underwent surgical treatment at FUSCC between 2008 and 2020. We integrated tumor size with clinicopathological characteristics to assess metastatic risk using machine-learning models and SHAP-based interpretation. By modeling tumor size as both a categorical and continuous variable, we further investigated its prognostic relevance using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression incorporating restricted cubic splines. Additionally, an independent cohort of 6,739 patients from Changhai Hospital was used for external validation. Machine-learning identified lymph node metastasis as the primary predictive endpoint, with the CatBoost model achieving the highest AUROC of 0.800. SHAP analysis showed that smaller tumor diameter contributed positively to predicted metastatic risk. Multivariable restricted cubic spline analysis further demonstrated a significant nonlinear association between tumor diameter and OS, with mortality risk increasing as tumor diameter decreased within the approximately 0-3 cm range. Among younger male patients with locally advanced disease, tumors ≤3 cm were associated with significantly worse OS and DFS than tumors >5 cm (both Smaller tumor size may paradoxically indicate higher lymph node metastatic risk and poorer prognosis in a subset of patients with colorectal cancer, particularly younger male patients with locally advanced disease. Tumor size may therefore serve as a complementary factor for postoperative risk stratification beyond conventional TNM staging.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, has attracted increasing attention in recent years because of its critical roles in tumor progression, therapeutic resistance, and immune regulation. Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide and imposes a substantial mortality burden. This study aimed to systematically analyze the global research landscape, hotspots, and developmental trends of ferroptosis in CRC research from 2017 to 2025. English-language publications related to ferroptosis and CRC published between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2025, were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus databases. A total of 1, 354 original articles and reviews were included. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the bibliometrix package in R were used for bibliometric and visualization analyses to evaluate annual publication trends, country/region and institutional collaboration networks, author contributions, journal distribution, co-cited references, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic evolution. The number of publications in this field increased rapidly after 2020 and peaked in 2025. China ranked first in both publication output and total citations, followed by the United States, and China-United States collaboration constituted the core of the international collaboration network. Central South University was the most productive institution, while journals such as Frontiers in Oncology and Frontiers in Immunology served as major publication platforms. Research hotspots were mainly concentrated on chemotherapy resistance, the tumor immune microenvironment, PANoptosis, prognostic models, non-coding RNAs, gut microbiota, and the regulation of ferroptosis by traditional Chinese medicine and natural products. Ferroptosis has become a rapidly evolving frontier in CRC research. The research focus is gradually shifting from fundamental molecular mechanisms toward translational medical directions, including chemosensitization, combination immunotherapy, reversal of drug resistance, and precise prognostic evaluation. This study provides a systematic reference for understanding the global knowledge structure and future research directions in the field of ferroptosis and CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a crucial imaging modality for the management of rectal cancer. Conventional MRI provides detailed anatomical information but has a limited capacity to evaluate tumor biology. Intravoxel Incoherent Motion (IVIM) is an advanced functional MRI technique that simultaneously measures tissue cellularity and microvascular perfusion without contrast agents, providing deeper insights into the tumor microenvironment. This narrative review critically examines the current evidence on the clinical usefulness of IVIM MRI in rectal cancer, focusing on three key areas: tumor characterization and staging, prediction and monitoring of treatment response, and the reproducibility and limitations of IVIM parameters. A literature search was conducted in vid MEDLINE, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and Google Scholar from 2015 to October 2025. The search included keywords such as "intravoxel incoherent motion OR IVIM" and "rectal cancer OR colorectal cancer." Original studies with at least 10 patients were included; reviews, case reports, and animal studies were excluded. The true diffusion coefficient D appears to be the most biologically interpretable and reproducible IVIM-derived parameter, with several studies linking lower D values to greater cellularity or more aggressive tumor features; however, findings are not uniform across all cohorts. While the perfusion fraction (f) has shown associations with markers of aggressiveness in some studies, its clinical utility is limited by poor reproducibility. For nodal staging, primary-tumor IVIM histogram models have shown promising diagnostic performance, although most evidence remains from single centers and is insufficiently validated. When assessing the response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT), a post-treatment increase in D appears to be the most consistent IVIM-derived marker of treatment response. However, its clinical use still requires standardized acquisition and external validation while perfusion parameters (f and D*) exhibit poor test-retest reproducibility. Combining IVIM with complementary techniques, such as diffusion kurtosis imaging or radiomics, may improve predictive performance compared with individual parameters. IVIM-DWI provides non-contrast quantitative information on diffusion and perfusion in rectal cancer. Current evidence suggests that D is the most reproducible and biologically interpretable IVIM parameter, whereas f and D* remain limited by poor repeatability and protocol dependence. IVIM may add value for tumor characterization, nodal risk assessment, and treatment-response evaluation, particularly when combined with histogram analysis, DKI, or radiomics; however, standardized acquisition protocols and external validation are required before routine clinical implementation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) has become a widely accepted technique for en bloc resection of colorectal laterally spreading tumors (LSTs). Although the procedure is generally considered safe, complications including bleeding and perforation may occur. The simultaneous development of pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, pneumoperitoneum, and extensive subcutaneous emphysema following colorectal ESD represents an exceptionally rare but potentially serious adverse event. A 56-year-old female patient underwent ESD for a granular-type LST measuring 8 mm × 20 mm located in the ascending colon. The procedure was performed under general anesthesia with tracheal intubation and carbon dioxide insufflation. Complete en bloc resection was achieved, and the post-ESD mucosal defect was closed with 16 titanium clips. Approximately 3 h after the procedure, the patient developed progressive neck swelling without respiratory distress or chest pain. Computed tomography (CT) revealed a small amount of pneumothorax on the right side and fluid pneumothorax on the left side (lung compression <10%), extensive subcutaneous emphysema involving the neck, chest wall, and right proximal thigh, pneumomediastinum, and pneumoperitoneum. The patient was managed conservatively with high-flow nasal cannula oxygen, bowel rest, intravenous antibiotics, and proton pump inhibitor therapy. Serial imaging demonstrated gradual resolution of the ectopic gas collections. The patient recovered uneventfully and was discharged on postoperative day 7. This case demonstrates that extensive gas extravasation involving multiple body compartments can occur as a rare complication of colorectal ESD, particularly when procedures are performed in the retroperitoneal portion of the colon under general anesthesia with positive pressure ventilation. Prompt recognition, timely CT evaluation, and conservative management in hemodynamically stable patients can lead to favorable outcomes without the need for surgical intervention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal adenocarcinoma is a significant health concern in Iraq, with variations in demographic and histopathological characteristics compared to global trends. This study retrospectively analysed 120 colorectal carcinoma cases from multiple medical centres in Iraq to assess patient demographics, pathological features, and disease staging. Data were gathered, and variables were examined statistically. The mean patient age was 58.6 years, with 35% of cases occurring in individuals under 50 years old, indicating a trend toward earlier onset. A slight male predominance was observed (54.2% male vs. 45.8% female). Tumour location was most frequently in the left colon (41.7%), followed by the right colon and rectum (29.2% each). Moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma was the most common histopathological type (66.7%), and 75% of patients presented with advanced disease stages (Stage II or III). Adverse prognostic factors, including lymphovascular invasion (37.5%), perineural invasion (25%), and tumour budding (16.7%), were also noted. The results underscore the need for enhanced screening programs and public health initiatives in Iraq to promote early detection and improve colorectal cancer outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the second most common cause of cancer-related death globally and the third most common type of cancer. This study aims to evaluate the prevalence of psychiatric morbidities after colorectal surgical procedures, identify associated risk factors for their development, and determine whether improved access to psychological therapies would benefit this patient population. Between January 2019 and December 2023, 603 patients with a diagnosis of colorectal disease underwent elective colorectal operations in our institution and were considered for this retrospective study. Data were collected from medical and operating theatre records as well as from the hospital-coded database. Patient data were primarily analysed for the incidence of colorectal diseases such as colorectal cancer, diverticulitis, and inflammatory bowel disease. Secondary variables include patient characteristics (age at operation, gender), length of hospital stay, and operative parameters (time and type). During the 5-year study period, a total of 603 records of patients operated on for colorectal disease in our institution were retrieved from the computer database. A total of 499 (83%) colectomies were performed using the open method, and 104 (17%) were performed using the laparoscopic technique. Among patients undergoing colorectal operation in our institution 126 (20.1%) had a psychiatric disorder in the one-year postoperative follow-up. The most common type of mental disorder was mood disorder, which appeared in 26 patients. This retrospective study shows that the technique of colectomy does not appear to affect the incidence of psychiatric disorders. However, our study indicates the need for a prospective randomised controlled trial with a larger number of participants.
