ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and vascular mural cells may shape extracellular matrix organization in colorectal cancer. However, single-cell comparisons are susceptible to unequal cell recovery, ambient RNA, doublets, treatment-stage mixing, and repeated sampling within patients. We investigated fibrovascular remodeling using patients as the inferential unit and distinguished reproducible signals from donor-concentrated and context-dependent findings. We reanalyzed a published single-cell RNA sequencing cohort of 22 patients, including 20 with colorectal cancer and 2 with duodenal carcinoma. The primary pericyte analysis included 14 pretreatment matched normal-tumor pairs with at least three pericytes per tissue. We assessed ambient contamination and doublets using DecontX and scDblFinder. CAFs were reclustered at six response-blind resolutions, and the stable parent population was tested by patient-blocked pseudobulk analysis after excluding its dominant donor. Independent CRC single-cell and spatial datasets, a cross-cancer immunotherapy cohort, and TCGA were used for external testing. After DecontX correction, tumor pericytes had higher ECM6 scores (median paired change 0.309; false discovery rate [FDR] 0.018). Scores were also higher for the matrix stiffness transcriptional proxy (0.277; FDR 0.012) and the hypoxia/angiogenesis transcriptional program (0.255; FDR 0.028). All three signatures remained significant at the five-pericyte threshold (n=13). COL1A1 and FN1 increased in the analysis, although COL1A1 was borderline in the five-cell sensitivity analysis. Response-blind stability analysis identified a 2,983-cell ECM-remodeling CAF population represented in all 22 patients. After excluding P02, patient-blocked pseudobulk analysis in 15 patients showed higher matrix, inflammatory, and myCAF-related programs and a lower iCAF program. Neither SPP1 nor baseline enrichment in stable disease was supported. In GSE205506, a disjoint 10-gene fibroblast gate retained higher inflammatory and composite CAF scores in non-pCR samples. The highest-scoring unsupervised cluster was donor-concentrated and showed no patient-level association with response. Spatial and cross-cancer analyses yielded mixed or null results. These results support pretreatment fibrovascular transcriptional remodeling at the patient level. They do not establish an SPP1-high response biomarker, a mechanical stiffness phenotype, or causal CAF-to-pericyte signaling. Donor-aware analysis places the rare-cluster observation within a broader, reproducible ECM-remodeling CAF program while defining its evidential limits.

Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a progressive cholestatic liver disease strongly associated with ulcerative colitis (UC). Although uncommon, PSC-associated ulcerative colitis (PSCUC) represents a distinct subtype of inflammatory bowel diseases characterized by a higher risk of colorectal and hepatobiliary cancers. Early diagnosis remains a challenging issue because of the lack of specific biomarkers. Bioinformatic analysis of Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets identified potential, specific, and noninvasive biomarkers via differential gene expression and functional enrichment. After processing the data, S100A8 and S100A12 were identified as candidate biomarkers for detecting PSC in patients with UC. S100A8 encodes one component of calprotectin, the S100A8/S100A9 heterodimer widely used as a marker of intestinal inflammation. These two genes are primarily involved in inflammation, immune responses, and leukocyte recruitment, making them potentially useful biomarkers for early detection in PSC in UC patients. These biomarkers offer potential implications for disease stratification and therapeutic targeting. Further validation in prospective clinical studies is warranted to confirm their diagnostic and prognostic utilities.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Joint modeling provides a robust statistical framework for simultaneously modeling longitudinal covariate and time-to-event outcome. Apart from the interdependence between longitudinal and survival outcomes there may exist some unobserved random heterogeneity which can be modeled using a joint frailty model (JFM). Unlike existing JFMs, where two survival events are modeled using a frailty, our framework incorporates frailty into the survival sub-model to accommodate an additional source of variation at the survival endpoint. So here we developed a novel JFM and estimated the parameters using maximum-likelihood estimation method. The analyses were performed using R Software and illustrated using colorectal cancer data. The frailty component was introduced in colorectal cancer data to account for the unobserved variability in survival risk beyond the observed clinical characteristics. The highly significant frailty variance confirmed the presence of unobserved heterogeneity in survival outcomes. When compared with the standard Joint model (JM), the JFM demonstrated improved model fit and captured additional unexplained heterogeneity among individuals, leading to more precise hazard estimates. Further we conducted Monte Carlo simulations to compare the performance of the proposed model under various simulation scenarios (censoring [20% and 50%], frailty variance (≈0, 0.5, 1), and sample sizes [n = 100, 250, 500]). Performance was assessed using bias, root mean squared error and model fit indices. The findings highlight the importance of incorporating the frailty term in joint modeling, particularly in cancer prognostic studies where individual heterogeneity plays a crucial role.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted cancer screening and diagnostic pathways globally. Aggregate screening-derived indicators require cautious interpretation because they do not represent confirmed cancer registry incidence but might reflect program participation, referral patterns, and denominator composition. To evaluate pre- and post-COVID-19 changes in selected solid cancer screening-derived incidence proxy rates in South Korea, and to estimate model-based proxy rates through 2028. This retrospective ecological longitudinal study analyzed publicly available aggregate annual cancer-screening statistics from the Korean National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) and Korean Statistical Information Service (KOSIS) for six solid cancer programs (stomach, liver, colorectal, breast, cervical, and lung cancer). Annual proxy rates per 100,000 screened or eligible persons were calculated. Pre-COVID (2010-2019) and post-COVID (2020-2024) means were compared using Welch t-tests with Mann-Whitney U sensitivity analyses. Ordinary least-squares (OLS) forecasts were generated for 2025-2028. Interrupted time-series analysis was not feasible owing to an insufficient post-COVID observation window. Post-COVID changes in proxy rates were heterogeneous across selected programs. Breast cancer proxy rates increased by 17.1% (Welch p = 0.002) and liver cancer proxy rates by 83.6% (Welch p = 0.002); the liver cancer increase reflects denominator restriction to a high-risk population rather than a true epidemiological surge. Stomach cancer decreased by 23.3% (Welch p = 0.001), cervical cancer by 56.9% (Welch p = 0.005), and colorectal cancer by 25.8% (Welch p = 0.007). Lung cancer data were available only from 2019 to 2024 (program inception) and were interpreted descriptively. Aggregate South Korean national screening data show pandemic-era temporal associations with heterogeneous changes in selected solid cancer program proxy rates. These findings support an indirect screening-disruption and ascertainment interpretation rather than causal proof of a direct COVID-19 effect on solid cancer incidence.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, and dysregulation of phosphoinositides signaling pathways plays a critical role in its pathogenesis. The involvement of Set Binding Factor 1 (SBF1; MTMR5), a pseudophosphatase of the myotubularin family in CRC, remains unexplored. This study compiled experimental and bioinformatics approaches to investigate the expression and potential relevance of SBF1 in CRC. Immunohistochemical analysis was performed on CRC tissue specimens and corresponding normal adjacent tissues (NAT), with estimation of SBF1 staining followed by statistical comparison. In parallel, bioinformatics assessed gene ontology and protein-protein interactions, and open CRC datasets were analyzed to assess SBF1 alterations, expression profiles, and survival associations. The results demonstrated a significant overexpression of SBF1 in CRC tissues compared with NAT. Bioinformatics revealed SBF1 as a partner within a functional network enriched in phosphoinositide metabolism. Bioinformatics identified SBF1 genetic alterations in approximately 5% of cases, and survival analysis indicated that wild-type SBF1 could be an unfavorable prognostic marker, as reflected by hazard assessment. Collectively, these findings provided the first experimental evidence that SBF1 is overexpressed in CRC and suggest that it may represent an unrecognized component of phosphoinositide related pathways involved in colorectal tumorigenesis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Low take rates and inter-tumor variability in growth rates can limit the effectiveness of mouse xenograft models when comparing between groups. To address this problem we developed a simple method to compare multiple cell types within a single mixed xenograft. Individual cell lines or clones were transduced with a lentiviral vector that includes a unique PCR tag, allowing the use of qPCR to determine the proportion of each tagged cell type within a mixed xenograft tumor. We generated vectors with six distinct PCR tags, and two different selectable markers, and have optimized the approach for determining their relative proportions within a mix. An initial pre-amplification step is used to increase the amount of material for subsequent qPCR reactions. This also removes the bulk of the genomic DNA, increasing the specificity of the qPCR step. Samples are then used for qPCR with specific pairs of primers that distinguish between each of the individual PCR tags, and the relative proportion of each tag is determined relative to that in the starting mix. We have tested this approach for in vitro growth of mixed cell cultures and in an orthotopic cecal xenograft model using a human colon cancer cell line. Since each individual tumor is initiated with a mix of cells, multiple tumors within a single animal can be analyzed separately, and overall tumor size is not important. Similarly, multiple metastatic lesions from the same animal can be analyzed individually. Thus, each tumor provides a direct comparison between individually tagged cell lines or clones. This low throughput "bar-coding" approach is simple and cost effective and has the potential to reduce the number of animals needed for xenograft experiments.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To evaluate the efficacy and safety of low-dose hypofractionated radiotherapy (LDHRT) for liver metastases when combined with immunotherapy. Patients with liver metastases receiving immunotherapy were enrolled in this study at Changzhou Second People's Hospital from January 2019 to May 2025 (Ethics Approval No. [2021]KY117-01). LDHRT (12 Gy in 3 fractions) was administered to the liver metastases using volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT). The tumor response was evaluated according to the RECIST 1.1 standard. Clinical and imaging data were collected to assess changes in tumors inside and outside the radiation field before and after LDHRT, as well as the median progression-free survival (PFS) for lesions within the radiation field. A total of 51 patients were included, with the median age of 69 (range 47-84) years; 86.3% (44/51) were male, and 94.1% (48/51) had an ECOG performance status (PS) score ≥1. Additionally, 54.9% (28/51) had received ≥3 lines of prior therapy. Due to the continuous progression of liver metastases under systemic treatment, LDHRT was administered for the liver metastases. The study found a high local control rate within the radiation field as the objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) within the radiation field were 17.6% and 86.3%, respectively. However, the efficacy for lesions outside the radiation field was significantly inferior, with an ORR of 0% and a DCR of 35.3%. The median PFS for lesions within the radiation field was 4.23 months. Patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) showed better PFS than those with gastric cancer liver metastases (GCLM). The most common adverse events were fatigue (16/51, 31.4%), abnormal liver function (11/51, 21.6%), and hypothyroidism (7/51, 13.7%). No patients discontinued treatment due to treatment-related adverse events. LDHRT combined with immunotherapy provided favorable local control and was generally well tolerated in patients with liver metastases. No apparent abscopal effect was observed, suggesting that single-lesion LDHRT was insufficient to reverse systemic immunosuppression.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Organised colorectal cancer (CRC) screening reduces mortality, yet participation routinely falls short of policy targets, a gap most acute in structurally disadvantaged, insular, and rapidly ageing populations. The Azores, an outermost European Union archipelago, exemplifies this challenge: CRC accounts for 10% of regional cancer diagnoses and is the second leading oncological cause of potential years of life lost, with 2024 mortality (24.9 per 100,000) exceeding mainland Portugal. Despite a mature organised screening programme (ROCCRA), archipelago-wide participation stands at just 30.3%, with roughly one in five residents who consent and receive a home test kit never returning it. This perspective article argues that conversational artificial intelligence based on large language models (LLMs), the current generation of natural language processing (NLP) technology, capable of understanding and responding to patient concerns in real time, represents a promising approach for bridging this gap. Because the barriers identified in the literature are well, inherently dialogic, an interactive, multi-channel conversational cascade is better suited to address cognitive and operational friction than static reminders. Specifically, this paper synthesises presumed drivers of non-adherence, inferred from the literature and considered likely to apply to the Azorean context, reviews the evidence supporting conversational and voice-enabled outreach in cancer screening, and uses regional data to model the potential impact of a well-targeted voice AI deployment. Beyond the Azores, this framework illustrates how NLP-enabled conversational AI could support more responsive, equitable, and scalable public health screening programmes in geographically dispersed and underserved populations.

Intraperitoneal metastasis is a frequent progression in colon cancer, highlighting the critical need for enhanced therapeutic approaches. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Malnutrition, altered body composition, and sarcopenia are common among patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) and are associated with poor treatment tolerance and adverse clinical outcomes. PhA, derived from BIA, reflects cellular membrane integrity and body cell mass and has been increasingly investigated as a potential marker of nutritional status and prognosis in oncology. However, the clinical relevance of PhA in patients with CRC has not yet been systematically synthesized. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for observational studies published between January 2000 and October 2025 that assessed PhA in adult patients with CRC. Data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment using the AXIS tool were performed independently by two reviewers. Due to substantial heterogeneity in study design, outcome definitions, and PhA cut-off values, a narrative synthesis was conducted. A total of 10 studies involving 1,439 patients were included. Lower PhA values were consistently associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Four studies reported significantly shorter overall or progression-free survival among patients with low PhA. Four studies demonstrated associations between low PhA and unfavorable short-term outcomes, including postoperative complications, prolonged hospital stay, cancer-related complications, and early chemotherapy-related toxicity. Several studies also reported positive associations between PhA and indicators of nutritional status, body composition, muscle mass, muscle strength, and hydration balance. One longitudinal study showed that postoperative increases in PhA were accompanied by improvements in body composition parameters and reduced early chemotherapy-related toxicity. Current evidence indicates that BIA-derived phase angle is associated with nutritional status, body composition, treatment tolerance, and survival outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer. However, heterogeneity in measurement protocols and cut-off values limits direct clinical application. Standardized assessment methods and prospective studies are needed to establish CRC-specific reference values and to determine whether interventions that improve PhA can translate into improved clinical outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Frailty is a degenerative geriatric syndrome characterized by declining muscle mass and function, unintentional weight loss, and fatigue. It is a key risk factor for many geriatric diseases and poor postoperative outcomes. Currently, pathogenesis remains unclear, and apart from nutritional support and exercise, no pharmacological interventions are available. Notably, the frailty phenotype is also a major feature in patients with advanced-stage cancer, and both frailty and advanced cancer are characterized by dysregulation of nutritional and energy metabolism. Consequently, cancer serves as a novel accelerated model for investigating the mechanisms underlying frailty development. The phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) framework was employed to systematically analyze the causal relationship between 264 cancer types and frailty, and to identify candidate cancer types directly causally associated with frailty. A large-scale analysis was conducted to assess the causal relationship between "candidate cancer- Icelandic peripheral blood proteome-frailty" and to further explore the characteristics and patterns of the key proteins mediating cancer-induced frailty using the two-sample Mendelian randomization method. Finally, the correlation between key candidate proteins and frailty was verified using peripheral blood from a 100-case colorectal cancer (CRC) cohort. The PheWAS analysis identified 21 cancer types with significant causal associations with frailty among the 264 cancers examined. An in-depth analysis of the top 5 cancer types revealed that the mechanisms by which they induce frailty exhibit both prominent shared features and distinct characteristics. Shared signaling pathways included stress responses, immune processes, and metabolic pathways. Among these, immune-related pathways involving complement component C3 (C3), lipocalin-2 (LCN2), and coagulation factor V (F5) emerged as key shared mechanisms across multiple cancer types. Finally, validation in an independent clinical cohort of patients with CRC ( This study systematically elucidated the causal relationships between cancer and frailty, identified multiple candidate proteins that may drive frailty progression, and demonstrated that complement C3 is associated with frailty development. Furthermore, we propose that cancer serves as a novel accelerated model for investigating the mechanisms underlying frailty. These findings provide new insights into the biological mechanisms underlying frailty and identify a series of promising molecular targets for future mechanistic studies and therapeutic interventions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain major diagnostic challenges because classification often depends on modality-specific evidence that is stored in separate public datasets. This study evaluates a dual-branch CNN-LSTM framework using two independent and unpaired data sources: colorectal histopathological image patches and structured HCC clinical-biochemical records. The study is therefore positioned as an exploratory investigation of representation learning across heterogeneous medical datasets. The CNN branch extracts spatial and glandular texture features from curated CRC image patches, whereas the LSTM branch treats fixed-order clinical attributes as a structured feature sequence to learn inter-feature dependencies in the HCC records. Under internal public-dataset testing with bootstrap uncertainty estimation, the full CNN + LSTM + MLP framework achieved an accuracy of 0.978 (95% CI, 0.971-0.984), Macro-F1 of 0.977 (95% CI, 0.971-0.984), and Macro OVR AUC of 0.997 (95% CI, 0.996-0.998). Ablation and baseline comparisons showed lower performance for CNN only (accuracy 0.938), LSTM only (0.875), clinical encoder only (0.890), CNN + LSTM (0.966), CNN + clinical MLP (0.958), late fusion (0.952), EfficientNet-B0-style fusion (0.970), ViT-tiny-style fusion (0.960), XGBoost (0.910), random forest (0.900), and logistic regression (0.875). The full model also exceeded the EfficientNet-B0-style baseline in Macro AUC by 0.003 (95% CI, 0.002-0.004; paired bootstrap P = 0.007; McNemar exact P = 0.011). Grad-CAM and SHAP analyses are used to interpret branch-specific decisions, while the findings remain limited to internal public-dataset validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is common in Western countries, about 50% of patients develop liver metastases (CLM). While local CLM therapies can achieve 5-year survival up to 60%, most patients eventually become unresectable (uCLM) and have poor outcomes with systemic treatment alone. Prospective studies, including SECA I and II and the TransMet trial, showed that in carefully selected patients, liver transplantation (LTx) can achieve survival outcomes comparable to standard LTx indications. The aim of this work was to develop a harmonized national consensus protocol for the indication and selection of uCLM patients eligible for LTx. Under the coordination of the Belgian Liver & Intestine Advisory Committee (Be-LIAC), all six Belgian transplant centers delegated a transplant surgeon, an oncologist and an hepatologist to a working group that performed a literature review and drafted preliminary criteria. Three successive national meetings and a structured voting refined these criteria in the current protocol. Consensus was reached on inclusion and exclusion criteria for LTx in uCLM. Two key conditions are liver-only disease and technically uCLM. Strict requirements include a six months disease stability or response on systemic therapy and an obligatory eight-week treatment holiday. Absolute CEA levels and specific somatic mutations are not excluded. A national Be-LIAC governance model was established, combining local prospective decision-making with central auditing and registry-based evaluation. A harmonized national protocol for LTx inuCLM has been established, ensuring consistent patient selection across all Belgian centers. Stricter criteria and a national governance model aim to optimize outcomes while maintaining ethical allocation of donor organs.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a formidable clinical challenge, largely due to the prevalence of microsatellite-stable tumors characterized by an immunologically "cold" tumor microenvironment (TME) that is resistant to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Tumor-derived exosomes (TEXs) play a paradoxical dual role in this landscape. Native TEXs actively orchestrate immune evasion by delivering immunosuppressive molecules, such as programmed cell death 1 ligand 1 (PD-L1) and transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β), which impair cytotoxic T-cell function and promote the expansion of regulatory T cells and M2 macrophages. Conversely, TEXs possess inherent biocompatibility and naturally harbor a broad repertoire of tumor-associated antigens (TAAs) and major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules, positioning them as potential cell-free platforms for cancer vaccination. Current evidence demonstrates that native TEXs establish their immunosuppressive niche primarily through the systemic PD-1/PD-L1 axis and microRNA-driven macrophage polarization. However, preclinical studies indicate that exosome engineering strategies-such as masking surface PD-L1 or loading vesicles with immune adjuvants, siRNAs, or CRISPR components-can effectively neutralize these suppressive traits and amplify antigen presentation. While clinical data in CRC remain limited, engineered TEXs exhibit strong preclinical promise for synergizing with ICIs to reprogram cold CRC into immune-responsive "hot" tumors. Advancing these early-stage therapies from the bench to the clinic will require overcoming significant translational hurdles, particularly regarding standardized isolation protocols and scalable manufacturing.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Splenic metastases usually historically signal pre-terminal malignancy, arising amid widespread tumor dissemination and most often discovered at autopsy. Isolated splenic metastases without disseminated disease are exceedingly rare, with only a limited number of cases reported in the literature. Recognizing these presentations is important as isolated splenic involvement may be amenable to definitive management in contrast to the poor prognosis associated with splenic spread. In this report, we present two patients with isolated splenic metastases. The first is an 83-year-old patient with splenic metastasis secondary to colorectal cancer. The second is a 29-year-old patient with splenic metastasis secondary to a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (PNET), which, to our knowledge, may represent a novel incidence. Neither patient had evidence of disseminated disease at presentation. In this case report, we review the clinical presentation, diagnostic workup, and management of both cases, each of which demonstrate a favorable short-term outcome. These cases taken together show that isolated splenic disease, when identified in the absence of widespread metastasis, can be operatively and chemically managed with favorable short-term results. The PNET patient in particular broadens the recognized spectrum of primary tumor locations that can metastasize to the spleen in isolation. Further reports and longer follow-ups, however, are needed to identify the optimal management and longer-term prognoses.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colitis cystica profunda (CCP) is a rare benign colorectal lesion characterized by mucus-filled cysts within the submucosa. However, the durability of endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) for CCP beyond 48 months has not been documented. This case aims to fill that gap. ESD has emerged as a minimally invasive approach enabling both definitive diagnosis and treatment, but data on long-term efficacy remain limited, with no reported follow-up exceeding 48 months. A 49-year-old woman presented with a 6-month history of unformed stools. Colonoscopy revealed a submucosal mound-like lesion in the rectum, 5 cm from the anal verge. Endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS) showed hypoechoic areas (0.4 cm × 0.2 cm) confined to the muscularis mucosa and submucosa, suspicious for a neuroendocrine tumor. Routine laboratory tests (complete blood count, C‑reactive protein, carcinoembryonic antigen) were within normal limits. ESD was performed for en bloc resection. Histopathological examination demonstrated cystica dilated glands in the submucosa lined by benign colonic epithelium with surrounding fibrotic stroma and chronic inflammatory infiltration, confirming the diagnosis of CCP. No cytologic atypia was observed. The patient was followed with serial colonoscopy at 12, 40, and 52 months post-ESD, and with contrast‑enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at 12 months. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Wexner Constipation Score (0/30) and 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) questionnaire (scores comparable to population norms). All follow‑up examinations showed stable scar‑like changes without evidence of recurrence, and the patient maintained normal bowel habits (formed stools 1-2 times daily). This case provides preliminary evidence that ESD can achieve durable remission and excellent functional outcomes in a single patient with CCP over 52 months. However, these findings are from one case and require confirmation in larger, prospective studies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Postoperative pain, opioid exposure and slow recovery remain common concerns in elderly patients undergoing laparoscopic radical resection of colorectal cancer. We assessed whether anterior quadratus lumborum block at the lateral supra-arcuate ligament (QLB-LSAL) combined with low-dose esketamine improves recovery quality. In this single-centre, randomized, placebo-controlled trial with blinded outcome assessment, 90 patients aged ≥60 years were assigned to QLB-LSAL with a saline infusion (Group Q), esketamine alone (Group E), or QLB-LSAL with esketamine (Group QE). The prespecified primary endpoint was the QoR-40 total score on postoperative day 3. Esketamine 0.2 mg/kg was given intravenously before induction, followed by 0.2 mg/kg/h until 30 min before the end of surgery in Groups E and QE; Group Q received an equal volume of saline. Longitudinal data were analysed with linear mixed-effects models, with Tukey post-hoc testing and Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Eighty-eight patients were analysed (Q=29, E=30, QE=29). On day 3 the QoR-40 total score was higher in Group QE than in Group E (adjusted difference 8.30, 95% CI 4.37-12.23, Tukey P<0.001); the corresponding day-1 difference was 12.07 (95% CI 7.66-16.47, P<0.001). Group QE also showed better comfort and pain scores, lower remifentanil consumption and fewer day-1 pump activations than Group E, and a higher day-1 QoR-40 score than Group Q (P=0.006). Between-group differences in HADS anxiety scores were not significant after adjustment for multiplicity (QE vs Q on day 1, P=0.068). The incidence of adverse events did not differ between groups. In elderly patients undergoing laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery, QLB-LSAL combined with low-dose esketamine improved the prespecified day-3 recovery endpoint and reduced early postoperative pain and opioid use compared with esketamine alone; any anxiolytic effect was not confirmed after multiplicity adjustment. Trial registration: ChiCTR2400082301.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Postoperative inflammatory-nutritional deterioration may adversely affect recovery after colorectal cancer surgery. This study aimed to develop and internally validate an interpretable machine learning model for preoperative prediction of postoperative modified Glasgow Prognostic Score (mGPS) = 2. This single-centre retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent elective radical resection for colorectal cancer between 2020 and 2025. The cohort was divided into training and internal validation sets using stratified sampling. Recursive feature elimination identified eight predictors: age, prealbumin, albumin, cholinesterase, lymphocyte percentage, platelet count, fibrinogen and serum calcium. Eight conventional machine learning algorithms, TabICLv2 and SuperLearner ensembles were evaluated using discrimination, calibration and decision curve analyses. SHapley Additive exPlanations were used for model interpretation. Among 1196 patients, 507 (42.4%) developed postoperative mGPS=2. In the internal validation cohort, TabICLv2 achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.753 (95% confidence interval, 0.701-0.804) and a Brier score of 0.197. SuperLearner-W and SuperLearner-SR showed comparable discrimination, with areas under the curve of 0.752 and 0.751, respectively. Lymphocyte percentage, platelet count and fibrinogen were the leading contributors to model predictions. Learning-curve analysis revealed suboptimal convergence behaviour, with relatively flat cross-validation trajectories and persistent separation from training performance across increasing training fractions. A web-based research prototype was developed to provide individualised risk estimates, patient-level feature attribution and an applicability-domain assessment indicating the level of support from the model-development data. An interpretable model based on routinely available preoperative variables provided moderate discrimination for postoperative inflammatory-nutritional deterioration after colorectal cancer surgery. The suboptimal learning-curve convergence indicates that the model is not suitable for clinical deployment without further development and independent external validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is associated with metabolic and inflammatory disturbances, including alterations in the arginine-nitric oxide (NO) pathway. This study assessed serum metabolites related to the arginine-NO-nitrated fatty acid (NO₂-FA) axis in patients with CRC and examined their associations with tumor stage and pathological features. A total of 122 patients undergoing colorectal resection for CRC were prospectively enrolled, of whom 117 had complete measurements for the candidate-metabolite panel and were included in the analyses. Preoperative serum samples were analyzed using targeted LC-MS/MS. Associations between metabolite concentrations and tumor stage were evaluated using complementary exploratory modelling approaches, including ordinal regression for TNM stage, tumor extent (T), and nodal involvement (N), as well as binary logistic regression for advanced disease (TNM III-IV), angioinvasion, and neuroinvasion. Among the analyzed metabolites, SDMA showed the most recurrent inverse association with pathological disease stage in the initial models. However, these associations attenuated after adjustment for age and sex and were further weakened after additional adjustment for serum creatinine, with all fully adjusted 95% confidence intervals (CIs) including unity. Thus, the observed SDMA pattern was not independent of renal function and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than as a convincing stage-associated metabolic signal. In a complementary binary analysis of TNM stages III-IV versus I-II, an inverse association with SDMA persisted after adjustment only under the stepwise selection strategy. Lower agmatine concentrations were associated with higher T category under the elastic-net strategy. Under the stepwise strategy, higher ADMA concentrations were associated with lower odds of angioinvasion and neuroinvasion, whereas higher citrulline concentrations were associated with higher odds of neuroinvasion. These invasive-feature associations were not reproduced under the elastic-net strategy and should therefore be considered procedure-dependent exploratory findings. No clear association was detected between circulating nitrooleates and the analyzed pathological outcomes. These exploratory findings identify preliminary stage-associated metabolic patterns within patients with CRC and require validation in independent cohorts.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA), a prevalent environmental contaminant found in food, water, and pharmaceuticals, is a recognized carcinogen strongly associated with colorectal cancer (CRC). However, the precise molecular mechanisms underlying NDMA-induced colorectal carcinogenesis remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to systematically investigate the molecular interactions between NDMA and CRC-related proteins to uncover potential mechanisms and therapeutic targets. We employed an integrated computational approach combining network toxicology and molecular docking. NDMA targets were identified using ChEMBL, STITCH, SwissTargetPrediction, and PharmMapper databases. CRC-associated genes were retrieved from GeneCards, OMIM, and TTD databases. Protein-protein interaction networks were constructed using STRING and analyzed with Cytoscape. Hub genes were identified through centrality analysis, validated using TCGA expression data, and subjected to molecular docking with AutoDock Vina. We identified 370 NDMA targets and 1,575 CRC-related genes, with 91 overlapping genes representing potential mediators of NDMA-induced carcinogenesis. Enrichment analysis revealed significant involvement of xenobiotic response, MAPK signaling, and extracellular matrix remodeling pathways. Network analysis identified TP53, HSP90AB1, and HSP90AA1 as critical hub genes, all showing significant differential expression in CRC tissues (p < 0.05). Molecular docking revealed direct binding of NDMA to TP53 (-4.2 kcal/mol), HSP90AB1 (-4.6 kcal/mol), and HSP90AA1 (-3.8 kcal/mol), suggesting potential functional interference beyond genotoxic effects. This study elucidates multi-faceted mechanisms of NDMA-induced colorectal carcinogenesis, identifying TP53, HSP90AB1, and HSP90AA1 as key molecular targets. The convergence of network analysis, expression validation, and structural predictions provides a comprehensive framework for understanding NDMA toxicity and offers potential targets for preventing CRC in exposed populations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To illuminate the role of liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) in colorectal cancer (CRC) and its potential as a therapeutic target, we conducted an in-depth analysis focusing on LLPS-related genes (LLPSRGs). Our approach involved a predictive model with LLPSRGs levels a s basis, with intent to prognosticate patient survival and assist in immunotherapy decision-making. Employing univariate Cox regression equipped with LASSO for initial screening, we identified LLPSRGs linked to CRC survival. A subsequent multivariate Cox regression analysis led to the establishment of a prognostic model that included seven pivotal genes. Survival analysis and ROC curve assessment confirmed the accuracy of this model in predicting CRC patient survival, validated in a GEO dataset. PPI network showed that there were complex correlations between differentially expressed genes in risk groups. qRT-PCR findings showed that the top 10 hub genes in the network were all upregulated in CRC cells. Immune profiling unveiled differences in immune cell infiltration and potential immunotherapy responses between high-risk and low-risk groups, with the latter being more suitable for immunotherapeutic interventions. Drug sensitivity analysis supported personalized treatment approaches. Overall, we developed a robust LLPSRG-based prognostic model for CRC, offering insights for CRC clinical prognosis and therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Medicinal mushrooms have higher metabolite content and thus receive considerable attention as medicines. Inonotus rickii (Pat.) Reid is one of the mushrooms found in India. The anticancer effects of I. rickii mushrooms were investigated in this study using breast cancer and colon cancer cell lines. I. rickii mushrooms are known to secrete exudate, and its cytotoxic effect on breast cancer cells (MDA-MB-231) and colon cancer cells (HCT116) was determined. Transcriptomic analysis was determined to investigate the differentially regulated genes responsible for the growth and migration of cancer cells. The cancer cells namely HCT116 and MDA-MB-231 cells were treated with 20% and 10% exudate of I. rickii for cell viability and wound healing assay was done. RNA from the treated and non-treated cells were isolated and analyzed for RNA sequencing. The RNA sequence data was analyzed for functional pathway enrichment analysis, data visualization and gene set enrichment analysis. Quantitative analysis of gene expression of some gene responsible for cancer inhibition by using real-time polymerase chain reaction. The culture exudate of I. rickii showed 25% decrease in cell viability of breast cancer cell line (MDA-MB-231) and colon cancer cell line (HCT116) at 10% (v/v) and 20% (v/v) of exudate respectively compared to HEK normal cell line. At low concentrations, comparative transcriptomics was performed after treatment of exudate to MDA-MB-231 and HCT116 cancer cells. Few differentially regulated genes included genes responsible for the growth and migration of cancer cells. The exudate treatment also showed inhibition in cell migration and also in genes involved in both the cancers. Thus, I. rickii exudate possess anti-cancer property based on cell viability, cell migration and gene expression analysis. Out of ten reported metabolites by LCMS analysis from exudate, four anticancerous metabolites viz., Kysimplexini, Pterulamide, Etzionin and Communesin H. Mushrooms are known to have many nutrients and thus can be used as a part of diet. Thus, these can be used as therapeutics for breast and colon cancer without any side effects.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The methodological and ethical analysis of clinical studies is a responsibility of the Research Ethics Committees. There are scenarios in which this assessment can be very difficult. This is the case with the TRASMETIR trial that studies liver transplantation in patients with unresectable metastases of colorectal carcinoma. It was conducted in several Spanish hospitals as a clinical trial because liver transplantation was not previously considered a treatment indication for these patients. To justify and supervise the trial, it was stated that it would not represent an additional financial burden for the hospitals and that it was a study based on routine clinical practice. Thus, the infrastructure and professionals dedicated to performing liver transplantation for approved indications could participate in this prospective clinical trial as if it were part of their ordinary work. Upon a detailed analysis of this new and interesting experience, we observed that there are ethical issues that require closer attention. These include the distinction between clinical practice and clinical studies, the impact of possible public sponsorship in clinical trials, the information received in order to participate in a trial by the different professional profiles that collaborate in the systematics of each transplant, the priority and availability of biological resources such as organs for transplantation for their integration into clinical trials, or the way in which information is given and the content of this information to the donor or relatives.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The development and progression of colorectal cancer (CRC) are closely associated with metabolic reprogramming, in which mitochondrial metabolism is critically associated with tumor cell survival and proliferation. This study aims to provide novel insights for mitochondrial metabolism-related genes (MMRGs)-based prognosis prediction, biomarker discovery, and the development of targeted therapeutic strategies in CRC. Based on multi-omics data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) (including single-cell RNA-seq), we systematically analyzed MMRGs through differential expression screening, functional enrichment, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression modeling, and independent validation, supplemented by cell-cell communication, immune infiltration, drug sensitivity, and regulatory network analyses. We identified 7 major cell types and uncovered the immune microenvironment characteristics in CRC patients. We constructed a novel MMRGs-centric prognostic signature (CD36/ACOX1) validated in TCGA and GEO cohorts, effectively stratifying patients into distinct risk groups with significant survival differences. The risk model demonstrated independent prognostic value, correlated with distinct immune landscapes and genomic features. Regulatory network analysis revealed miRNA/TF interactions targeting CD36/ACOX1, while drug sensitivity screening identified 81 therapeutic agents with enhanced efficacy in high-risk patients. Pseudotime trajectory analysis further uncovered novel B-cell differentiation dynamics associated with prognostic gene expression. The mitochondrial metabolic signature CD36/ACOX1 enables robust survival stratification in CRC. This clinically applicable model informs tumor microenvironment dynamics and precision oncology frameworks for CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Adenoma miss rates (AMRs) reduce the effectiveness of colonoscopy in preventing colorectal cancer (CRC). Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are being developed to address this limitation. This article reviews current evidence on their performance, prevention potential, real-world implementation, and cost-effectiveness, while offering practical guidance for gastroenterologists. A comprehensive literature search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and Cochrane Library databases from January 2015 to February 2026. All studies focusing on AI on colonoscopy and major society position statements were all included. Evidence was synthesized thematically with critical appraisal and clinical contextualization. Pooled data from meta-analyses confirms an approximately 20% relative increase in adenoma detection rate (ADR) and an approximately 50% relative reduction in AMR with computer-aided detection (CADe). ENDOANGEL demonstrated the highest efficacy in one network meta-analysis [odds ratio (OR) 1.84], followed by EndoAID (OR 1.64), though system rankings vary across analyses and should be interpreted with caution. Benefits are most prominent with diminutive early lesions, with limited impact on advanced adenomas or serrated lesions. A significant efficacy-effectiveness gap can however be seen between trial and real-world settings, driven by alert fatigue, Hawthorne effects, and endoscopist variability. Cost-effectiveness has been demonstrated in modeling studies conducted in European and American settings, with incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) ranging from EUR 23,000 to USD 122,539 per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) depending on the healthcare context. Implementation barriers remain substantial, consisting of organizational, technical, educational, and equity factors. AI systems have demonstrated measurable improvements in adenoma detection metrics in controlled trial settings; however, current evidence is insufficient to support a definitive conclusion about enhanced colonoscopy quality, and guidelines reflect ongoing uncertainty given uncertainty about long-term outcomes, real-world effectiveness and the balance of benefits with harms. Prospective trials with cancer incidence endpoints are essential to guide wider adoption.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Mechanical high-intensity focused ultrasound releases tumor antigens and danger signals. It provides a potential substrate for immune checkpoint blockade. However, antigen release does not necessarily generate productive dendritic cell priming. In colorectal cancer, this transition occurs within a mucosal microenvironment shaped by epithelial barrier integrity, microbial exposure and myeloid clearance. Neutrophils can support epithelial repair or reinforce tumor-associated suppression. Macrophages remove apoptotic granulocytes and regulate inflammatory resolution. They can also restrain dendritic cell cytokine production. These context-dependent functions may determine whether mechanically released antigens initiate cytotoxic immunity or enter a nonproductive clearance response. This mini review integrates intestinal myeloid homeostasis with experimental evidence for mechanical ultrasound ablation and PD-1/PD-L1 blockade. It distinguishes antigen uptake from cross-presentation, protective resolution from tumor-permissive suppression, and colorectal evidence from observations in other tumor models. Functional dendritic cell readouts, lineage-resolved checkpoint measurements and concurrent barrier assessment provide a framework for evaluating combination therapy. The therapeutic objective is to preserve mucosal protection while sustaining antigen-specific immunity.

Mechanisms of immune resistance in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer.
Frontiers in Oncology · 2026 · Niu D, Liu P, Chen X, Li J, Sun Z, Kuang Z, et al.
意义与启示：系统梳理MSS型结直肠癌免疫抵抗的多层次机制，为将“冷肿瘤”转化为免疫敏感微环境提供理论框架与治疗靶点启示。

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Microsatellite-stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC) accounts for approximately 85% of all CRC cases and exhibits limited responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), representing a major challenge in current cancer immunotherapy. At the tumor-cell intrinsic level, low tumor mutational burden (TMB), impaired neoantigen generation, aberrant activation of oncogenic pathways such as WNT/β-catenin signaling, and defects in interferon-γ signaling contribute to impaired immune recognition and immune escape. Within the TME, the accumulation of immunosuppressive populations, including regulatory T cells (Tregs), myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), and tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), together with extracellular matrix remodeling and chemokine dysregulation, establishes an immune-excluded microenvironment that restricts effective antitumor immune responses. Furthermore, metabolic alterations, including enhanced glycolysis, lactate accumulation, and amino acid metabolic reprogramming, impair immune cell function and promote immunosuppression. Epigenetic modifications, including DNA methylation, histone remodeling, and non-coding RNA regulation, further contribute to the silencing of immune-related genes and reinforcement of immune evasion. In addition, recent advances in single-cell sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have provided unprecedented insights into the cellular heterogeneity and spatial organization of MSS CRC immune ecosystems. This review summarizes current knowledge regarding the molecular and cellular mechanisms driving immune resistance in MSS CRC and discusses future therapeutic opportunities for transforming immunologically "cold" MSS tumors into responsive immune microenvironments.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Perilla frutescens, an edible medicinal plant from East Asia, produces diverse bioactive phytochemicals with anticancer activity, including perillaldehyde (PAH), rosmarinic acid (RA), luteolin, apigenin, and alpha-linolenic acid (ALA). These compounds exert multi-target anticancer effects through apoptosis, autophagy, and ferroptosis. PAH triggers ferroptosis in gastric cancer via the System Xc-/GSH/GPX4 axis and P62-Keap1-Nrf2 pathway, while inducing protective autophagy in colorectal cancer through SRD5A1 and PI3K/AKT modulation. RA directly binds KRAS(G12C) and suppresses NSCLC via KRAS/AKT/ERK, and inhibits stress-induced TNBC metastasis through Src inactivation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
B7-H3 (CD276), a member of the B7 family of immunoregulatory ligands, has emerged as an important molecule at the intersection of tumor biology and cancer immunology. Although initially identified as a regulator of T-cell responses, accumulating evidence supports its predominantly immunosuppressive role. B7-H3 is highly expressed across diverse malignancies, including brain, prostate, lung, breast, colorectal, and pediatric cancers, while showing limited expression in most normal adult tissues. Its tumor-associated expression, including tumor vasculature, makes B7-H3 an attractive therapeutic target. Beyond immune regulation, B7-H3 promotes tumor progression through tumor cell-intrinsic mechanisms involving PI3K/AKT, NF-κB, and STAT3 signaling, angiogenesis, epithelial-to-mesenchymal plasticity, and metabolic reprogramming. Within the tumor microenvironment, B7-H3 suppresses T-cell and natural killer cell activity and promotes immunosuppressive macrophage polarization, while its expression can be regulated by metabolic and epigenetic mechanisms. These multifaceted functions have stimulated the development of diverse B7-H3-targeted therapies, including monoclonal antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, CAR T-cell and Vδ1 T-cell therapies, nanobody-based platforms, and bispecific or trispecific immune cell engagers. Early clinical studies have demonstrated promising antitumor activity, although important challenges regarding efficacy, safety, tumor heterogeneity, and patient selection remain. In this review, we summarize the molecular regulation and biological functions of B7-H3, critically evaluate the current development of B7-H3-targeted therapies, and discuss key challenges and future directions for translating B7-H3-directed strategies into effective cancer treatments.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)-derived compounds have anticancer potential because of their multi-component, multi-target actions and generally favorable toxicity profiles. Clinical translation, however, is limited by poor aqueous solubility, rapid systemic metabolism, and insufficient tumor-selective delivery. This review critically evaluates recent TCM-based nanoformulations developed to address these limitations and improve the therapeutic performance. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) and EQUATOR guidance, PubMed and Web of Science databases were searched for original studies published during the previous 5 years using terms including "TCM," "nanoformulation," and "anticancer." After screening 387 records, 81 studies covering 50 representative TCM compounds were included and assessed for the preparation methods, antitumor mechanisms, and translational barriers. Relative to free compounds, nanoformulations frequently improved solubility, stability, apparent bioavailability, or the targeting efficiency of TCM constituents. Reported mechanisms included apoptosis, cell-cycle arrest, ferroptosis, immunogenic cell death, and tumor-microenvironment remodeling across breast, lung, colorectal, and other cancer models. Nevertheless, most evidence was derived from TCM-based nanoformulations represent a promising strategy for integrating traditional herbal medicine with modern cancer therapy. Despite these promising findings, substantial challenges remain in standardization, reproducibility, pharmacokinetics, long-term safety, manufacturing, and clinical validation. Future studies should prioritize head-to-head comparisons, quantitative biodistribution, clinically relevant models, and scalable manufacturing.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Intratumoral microbiota are emerging as important ecological components of the colorectal cancer (CRC) microenvironment. However, their stage-associated patterns and coordination with host gene expression remain poorly understood. This study aimed to characterize stage-associated associations between intratumoral microbiota and the host transcriptome in CRC. We profiled 73 regional tumor specimens from 30 independent, treatment-naïve CRC patients using full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing and mRNA sequencing. Microbial diversity, predicted functional profiles, co-occurrence networks, differential abundance, and microbiota-host transcriptome associations were analyzed. Regularized canonical correlation analysis and machine-learning modeling with SHAP-based feature interpretation were performed to identify stage-discriminative features. Candidate associations were evaluated in two independent public microbiome datasets. Mendelian randomization and immune-infiltration analyses were further conducted to explore the potential biological relevance of representative microbiota-gene associations. Disease stage was a major factor shaping intratumoral microbial composition. Advanced-stage CRC exhibited increased microbial α-diversity, distinct predicted functional profiles, and altered microbial co-occurrence patterns. Integrated microbiota-transcriptome analysis identified ten genus-level and six species-level candidate microbiota-gene association pairs. Core genera showed reproducible stage-discriminative signals in two independent public microbiome datasets. SHAP analysis identified the principal microbial and host transcriptomic features contributing to stage classification. Integrating microbial and host gene signatures improved classification performance, with the combined model achieving an AUROC greater than 0.90. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Mismatch repair (MMR) deficiency is uncommon in gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (GEP-NETs), yet it represents a critical biomarker for immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) eligibility. Treatment-associated reduction or loss of MMR protein expression, often without corresponding MSI-H, has been reported in colorectal adenocarcinoma, but comparable changes have not been described in neuroendocrine tumours. Persistent discordance between immunohistochemistry (IHC)-based MMR protein assessment and next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based microsatellite instability (MSI) testing is an emerging and clinically challenging phenomenon. We report a 55-year-old woman initially diagnosed with rectal NET Grade 1 on endoscopic biopsy; the tumour was upgraded to NET Grade 2 (Ki-67 approximately 20%) on the surgical resectionk specimen. Hepatic metastases were confirmed four months after resection. The first liver biopsy (January 16, 2026) demonstrated partial MMR protein loss by IHC (MLH1-, MSH2+, MSH6-, PMS2-), while concurrent NGS showed microsatellite stability (MSS) and a tumour mutational burden (TMB) of <1 mut/Mb. The patient received two cycles of surufatinib 250 mg orally once daily combined with intravenous carboplatin (500 mg, day 1) and etoposide (160 mg, days 1-3). Restaging CT demonstrated disease progression. A repeat liver biopsy (March 17, 2026) revealed complete loss of all four MMR proteins by IHC (MLH1-, MSH2-, MSH6-, PMS2-), while NGS again confirmed MSS and TMB <1 mut/Mb. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of apparent progressive complete MMR protein loss in the context of sequential platinum-based chemotherapy in metastatic rectal NET Grade 2, with persistent IHC-NGS discordance throughout. These findings raise an important question regarding how IHC-defined dMMR should be interpreted in the absence of NGS-confirmed MSI-H, and highlight the complexity of immunotherapy eligibility decisions in rare tumour types. Prospective data are needed to guide clinical practice.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden. Chemotherapy is central to the management of advanced or metastatic disease and is also used in perioperative settings, but outcomes vary substantially. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is an inexpensive and readily available marker of systemic inflammation; its prognostic association in chemotherapy-treated CRC warrants focused evaluation. This study adhered to PRISMA guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to July 15, 2025. Studies evaluating pretreatment NLR in relation to overall survival (OS) or a secondary progression- or recurrence-related time-to-event outcome, including progression-free survival (PFS), disease-free survival (DFS), or recurrence-free survival (RFS), in chemotherapy-treated CRC patients were eligible. Study screening, data extraction, and quality assessment were independently conducted by two reviewers. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models. Subgroup and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed. Thirty-eight studies (41 cohorts; 11,346 patients) were included. Elevated pretreatment NLR was associated with poorer OS (HR = 1.68, 95% CI 1.54-1.84; P < 0.0001) and poorer progression- or recurrence-related survival (HR = 1.61, 95% CI 1.43-1.81; P < 0.0001). The direction of association was generally consistent across exploratory subgroups defined by treatment category, age, geographic region, and NLR cut-off. Leave-one-out analyses did not identify a single study that changed the direction of either pooled association. Between-study heterogeneity and evidence of small-study effects warrant cautious interpretation. Elevated pretreatment NLR was associated with poorer survival outcomes in chemotherapy-treated CRC. NLR may be a readily available prognostic biomarker, but heterogeneous populations, variable outcome definitions and cut-off values, inconsistent covariate adjustment, and possible small-study effects currently limit its use for clinical decision-making. Prospective validation and methodological standardization are required before routine application. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251136904.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction (POGD) and Postoperative gastrointestinal intolerance (POGI) remain a critical challenge in abdominal surgery, particularly for colorectal cancer patients undergoing laparoscopic procedures. Current evidence suggests anesthetic agents may influence gastrointestinal recovery, yet the impact of esketamine remains underexplored. This trial aimed to investigate whether intraoperative esketamine administration accelerates gastrointestinal function recovery. In this single-center, randomized, outcome-assessor -blind trial, 104 patients (aged 18-75, ASA I-III) scheduled for elective laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery were allocated to receive either intravenous esketamine (0.2 mg/kg) or saline (control) 30 minutes before surgery completion. Primary outcome was time to first flatus; secondary outcomes included I-FEED scores, defecation time, oral intake tolerance, and postoperative complications assessed within seven days after surgery. The esketamine group demonstrated significantly shorter time to first flatus (52 [50.25-53.75] vs 60 [58.59-61.41] hours; P < 0.001) and first defecation (87 [81.96-92.04] vs 95 [92.65-97.35] hours; P = 0.04) compared to controls. I-FEED scores were markedly lower (median 1 [0.25-2] vs 2.5 [1-3]; P < 0.001), with reduced nausea (P = 0.001) and abdominal distension duration (P < 0.001). Esketamine also improved postoperative sleep quality, but did not affect hospitalization costs or length of stay. Intraoperative esketamine accelerates gastrointestinal function recovery after laparoscopic colorectal surgery, especially reducing postoperative gastrointestinal intolerance symptoms of nausea and distension while improving early sleep quality. However, no evident benefit was observed in reducing hospital length of stay or patient costs.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Food insecurity arising from insufficient access to food necessary for an active and healthy lifestyle is a prevalent yet underrecognized predictor of health that can increase the risk of chronic disorders. The impact of food insecurity on mortality rates from digestive tract diseases within the United States was analyzed. County-level age-standardized mortality rates for digestive tract diseases, encompassing both gastrointestinal tract and liver diseases, were obtained for 2015-2020 and linked to corresponding county-level measures of food insecurity, access to stores, enrollment in food programs, and other local variables. Separate analyses were performed for cancer and for noncancer conditions. Mortality rates from digestive diseases were significantly higher in counties within the highest compared to those with the lowest quintile of food insecurity. These associations remained positive when assessed separately for gastrointestinal tract or liver diseases, or for cancers and noncancer diseases. Food insecurity was associated with mortality from some cancers such as primary liver and colorectal cancers, but not for others such as esophageal or gallbladder cancer. Within food-insecure regions, factors such as younger age, population size and health, health care access, and economic factors were related to higher rates. Composite measures of social vulnerability or deprivation could identify locations with higher mortality. Food insecurity has a significant and detrimental association with mortality rates from digestive tract diseases. These findings emphasize the need to address food access with targeted interventions and for research on disease-specific impacts as crucial determinants of disease-related outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Background: Nucleosome positioning and occupancy are fundamental features of chromatin organization, yet their variation across human cancers and potential utility for noninvasive cancer detection remain poorly characterized. Methods: We systematically characterized nucleosome organization across 410 primary tumors spanning 23 cancer types using ATAC-seq, establishing a high-confidence pan-cancer nucleosome atlas validated by independent MNase-seq data. We characterized shared and cancer-type-enriched nucleosome patterns, investigated their associations with tumor heterogeneity and regulatory alterations, and evaluated tissue-derived nucleosome signatures for cancer classification and detection using circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA). Results: The atlas identified shared and cancer-type-enriched nucleosomes associated with distinct regulatory programs. Notably, nucleosome occupancy provided information complementary to chromatin accessibility for tumor stratification and revealed molecular heterogeneity within individual cancers, including subgroups associated with Basal-like breast cancer. In hepatocellular carcinoma, differential nucleosome analysis revealed cancer-associated chromatin remodeling involving regulatory pathways, transcription factor motifs, and candidate genes. Importantly, tissue-derived nucleosome signatures were detectable in cfDNA, enabling classification among three cancer types (AUROC = 0.877) and colorectal cancer detection (AUROC = 0.930), with an AUROC of 0.773 in an independent validation cohort. We also developed OncoNucAtlas, a publicly accessible database facilitating exploration of these nucleosome landscapes. Conclusions: Our study cancer-associated nucleosome organization as a complementary source of epigenomic information and demonstrates the potential of tissue-derived nucleosome signatures for cfDNA-based cancer detection. The pan-cancer atlas provides a resource for investigating tumor heterogeneity and developing noninvasive cancer detection approaches.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Deciphering cell niches in complex tissues is essential for understanding tissue structure and disease. Recent advances in spatial omics have enabled subcellular resolution and accurate cell identity mapping. However, robust delineation of cell niches and disease-associated spatial patterns remains difficult. We introduce Harmonics, a novel computational framework that systematically identifies both common and condition-specific cell niches from spatial omics data through hierarchical distribution matching. Harmonics also includes a suite of downstream modules that facilitate comprehensive niche characterization. We demonstrate its scalability, accuracy and generalizability across datasets spanning diverse species, tissues, diseases, spatial modalities, and technological platforms. For condition-agnostic datasets, Harmonics outperforms baseline methods in both accuracy and robustness, and further demonstrates the capability to resolve niche structures at finer granularity. Across diverse diseases including pulmonary fibrosis, triple-negative breast cancer, and colorectal cancer, Harmonics enables precise identification of condition-specific niches and reveals disease-associated dynamics, subtype-specific spatial patterns, and structured immune architectures. We envision Harmonics as a practical and versatile tool for spatial niche analysis that can be applied across a wide range of biological contexts and seamlessly integrated with existing spatial omics workflows.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Leucine-rich repeat-containing G protein-coupled receptor 5 (LGR5) is a marker of cancer stem-like cells frequently upregulated in colorectal cancer (CRC) with lower expression in normal tissues, making it a favorable target for antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). ADCs combine antibody specificity with potent cytotoxic payloads to enhance efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity. LGR5-targeting ADCs incorporating different payloads demonstrate strong initial tumor inhibition, yet tumors eventually recur due in part to LGR5 downregulation, necessitating more effective strategies to prevent relapse. We show treatment with chemotherapies or an LGR5-targeting ADC coupled to a topoisomerase 1 inhibitor payload (8E11-CPT2) reduces LGR5 levels and increases MET receptor expression and/or activation in CRC cells, supporting a therapeutic approach to target LGR5 and MET simultaneously. Accordingly, we engineered a MET-targeting ADC (ABT-700-SG3199) via site-specific conjugation of the anti-MET antibody telisotuzumab (ABT-700) with the DNA-crosslinking pyrrolobenzodiazepine (PBD) dimer SG3199. ABT-700-SG3199 exhibited superior potency and efficacy in CRC models compared to the clinical-stage MET-targeting ADCs ABBV-399 and ABBV-400, which use the same antibody backbone conjugated to different payloads. Treatment with ABT-700-SG3199 increased LGR5 expression, and the combination of ABT-700-SG3199 with 8E11-CPT2 enhanced CRC cell-killing efficacy, reinforcing the rationale for a dual-targeting approach. In patient-derived xenografts, combined administration of 8E11-CPT2 and ABT-700-SG3199 markedly delayed tumor relapse and prolonged survival compared with single-agent treatment. Taken together, these findings reveal a reciprocal regulation between MET and LGR5 in response to LGR5- or MET-targeting ADCs in CRC models and support a LGR5/MET dual-targeting therapeutic strategy to enhance efficacy and potentially overcome resistance and relapse.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
BackgroundCurrent British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) guidelines misclassify metachronous lesion risk after polypectomy in approximately 40% of patients. Building on evidence that immune exclusion drives progression of adenomas to colorectal cancer, this study examined immune profiles in screen-detected adenomas as a predictive biomarker for metachronous lesion risk. MethodsPatients undergoing polypectomy within the Scottish Bowel Screening Programme, with surveillance colonoscopy between 6 months and 6 years were included (n=2642). Chromogenic immunohistochemistry (IHC; n=2466), 6-plex multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF; n=331), and spatially resolved 6000-plex single cell transcriptomics (n=7) were applied to adenoma microarrays. Cell density and location were measured using QuPath. Hierarchical then K-means clustering was used to define immune cell density-based clusters, which were compared to future lesion events using Kaplan-Meier curves and the log rank test. ResultsAfter adjustment for age, sex, site, size and dysplasia, adenoma CD3+ T cell density was significantly associated with future colorectal neoplasia (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.20-1.72, p<0.001). Using mIF three immune cell density clusters were identified; 1) high T cell density, low macrophage density, 2) low T cell density, low macrophage density, and 3) high T cell, macrophage and SMA density, with significant differences in future lesion risk (Cluster 1: 22%, Cluster 2: 41%, Cluster 3: 36%, p=0.032). Bulk RNAseq and spatial transcriptomic analysis revealed significant variation in T cell and macrophage co-location and gene expression profiles between clusters. ConclusionAdenoma immune contexture emerges as a possible determinant of future metachronous lesion risk, offering a novel biomarker to refine surveillance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) enables molecular-resolution imaging of intracellular environments, but is constrained by the need to generate electron-transparent sections of the biological specimen and thus a limited imaging volume. To alleviate such limitations, we present a multiscale correlative workflow that links cryo-confocal fluorescence microscopy (cryo-FLM), cryo-focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (cryo-FIB-SEM) volume imaging (cryo-vEM), and cryo-FIB serial lamellae lift-out for cryo-ET in high-pressure frozen voluminous specimens. An integral part of this workflow is a sample holder that preserves specimen orientation across instruments, reduces manual handling, and overcomes stage-tilt limitations in cryo-FIB-SEM hardware. Applied to vitrified colorectal cancer organoids, we demonstrate that this workflow enables fluorescence-guided site preparation for cryo-vEM, which provides biological context beyond the limited field of view of cryo-ET, and targeted lift-out for fabrication of multiple lamellae from defined regions of interest. The reconstructed tomograms reveal subcellular architecture and cell-cell interfaces. This workflow establishes a modular methodological framework for continuum-resolution cryogenic imaging of complex 3D biological specimens.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer incidence in adolescents and young adults (AYAs; 18-39 years) is rising, but how their tumors differ genomically from those of older adults (OAs) is unclear. We analyzed paired tumor-normal whole-genomes from 698 AYAs and 5,220 OAs, with subcohorts matched by cancer group to disentangle age from tumor type. AYA tumors carried fewer somatic variants yet largely shared the same genetic drivers; many apparent age differences reflected age-dependent cancer subtypes, such as IDH-mutant glioma and HPV-positive cervical cancer. Colibactin, APOBEC and homologous recombination deficiency-associated signatures were more prevalent in AYA colorectal, gynecological and breast cancers, respectively, but were not more mutagenic when present, suggesting earlier-life activity rather than AYA-specific mutagenesis. Tumor type-concordant pathogenic germline variants were enriched in AYAs (10.9% overall versus 6.6% in matched OAs; p=0.006), often with a somatic second hit. Age thus shaped AYA cancer genomes through mutational processes, subtype composition and germline predisposition, supporting comprehensive tumor-normal profiling beyond driver-focused testing.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
KRAS mutations, including G12D, G12V and G13D, are major oncogenic drivers in colorectal cancer (CRC) and are associated with therapeutic resistance. However, approved KRAS inhibitors remain focused on G12C subtype, leaving these prevalent variants without approved targeted therapies. Here, we developed a lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based RNA interference (RNAi) strategy to target these three KRAS variants using a single small interfering RNA (siRNA) sequence. The developed siRNA-LNPs reduced KRAS mRNA and protein expression in HCT116 (G13D), SW620 (G12V) and LS180 (G12D) cells, but not in KRAS wild-type HT29 cells, suppressing the cellular proliferation, clonogenic survival and migration. Transcriptomic profiling revealed changes in KRAS associated signalling, including suppression of cell-cycle and DNA repair programmes, providing a rationale for combining siRNA silencing with the fluoropyrimidine chemotherapeutic agent 5-fluorouracil (5-FU). The combination produced synergistic effects across all three KRAS-mutant CRC cell models and enhanced the apoptosis in both monolayer cultures and 3D spheroids. Collectively, these findings provide proof of concept for this combination strategy and support its further investigation as a potential therapeutic approach for KRAS-mutant CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Spatial transcriptomics has identified AIF1, LIF, MRC1, and TNC as enriched in tumor budding (TB) regions of colorectal cancer. We investigated whether this TB associated gene module could be detected in bulk transcriptomic data. Pairwise gene co-occurrence was analyzed in bulk RNA-seq (TCGA-COADREAD, n=547) and single-cell RNA-seq (GSE178341, n=26,057 cells) using Fisher's exact tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. In bulk RNA-seq, pairwise fold-enrichments were weak (1.16 to 2.72), with AIF1 to LIF showing no significant association (FE=1.16, FDR=0.31). In single-cell data, the same pairs showed 31 to 184.5 fold enrichment (all FDR < 8e-38). Total UMI counts provided no evidence of doublet artifacts explaining these co-detection patterns. Exploratory enhancer-promoter interaction analysis in HCT116 cells further suggested these genes are controlled differently. GOT1 and MDH1, two malate-aspartate shuttle genes, showed lower expression in late-stage CRC (FDR less than or equal to 0.010). A bulk-derived risk score showed a modest association (Cox HR=1.21, p=0.021). Overall, TB-associated co-expression was more clearly detected at single-cell than bulk resolution, highlighting the importance of transcriptomic resolution when studying tumor-microenvironment-associated gene signatures.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Mass spectrometry-based metabolomics is essential for deciphering human metabolic functions and metabolite dark matter. However, the dark matter of the human metabolome is intricately hidden. Therefore, we developed MassBank Human, a curated library that distills 36,512,540 MS2 spectra from 76 public human datasets into 203,886 high-quality spectra via spectral averaging, recalibration, and filtering to achieve high mass accuracy. We further used three metabolite annotation tools and developed a Zipf-Bayesian rank aggregation framework to aggregate their rankings with false discovery rate control. This framework assigned molecular formulas, chemical classes, and planar structures to 55,564, 22,619, and 14,198 spectra, respectively. Approximately half of the annotated structures potentially originated from food, pollutants, or gut microbiota. In a metabolome analysis of colorectal cancer cells, MassBank Human doubled structural annotation coverage (10.6% to 21.2%), identifying acetylated polyamines as markers of metabolic rewiring. This community resource provides an annotated foundation for exploring human metabolomes.
