ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
PURPOSE: To develop and validate an artificial intelligence-enabled platform that combines efficient screening with explicit eligibility logic by converting unstructured cancer trial criteria into reusable structured queries, and illustrates potential eligibility using synthetic patients. METHODS: We downloaded actively recruiting US interventional treatment trials for advanced/metastatic breast cancer, colon cancer, and non-small cell lung cancer from ClinicalTrials.gov. Medical oncologists created 24 synthetic patient vignettes. A large language model converted trial eligibility criteria into Structured Query Language (SQL) code and patient information into structured records, enabling rule-based matching without further LLM inference. Cancer details and treatment history were considered, but not laboratory results or comorbidities. Validation included physician editing of generated eligibility code for 30 trials and independent assessments by two physicians, followed by consensus adjudication, for eligibility across ten trials. We descriptively summarized potential eligibility by trial characteristics and when varying age, ECOG performance status, sex, and ZIP code. RESULTS: Of 833 candidate trials, 746 met inclusion criteria. Performing matching for all 746 trials took a median of 0.459 seconds per patient, excluding patient-data preparation. Against physician consensus, automated matching agreed on 230/240 patient-trial pairs (95.8%; sensitivity 83.3%, specificity 100%). Across synthetic patients, potentially eligible trials ranged from 10 to 258 without geographic restrictions. Counts decreased with worse performance status and geographic restriction and were relatively stable across ages 30-90. Later-phase, randomized, and molecularly selective trials generally matched fewer vignettes. CONCLUSION: LLM-generated SQL enables rapid, explicit rule-based screening for potential trial eligibility. Evaluation in synthetic vignettes supports feasibility, while missed matches underscore the need for further validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immune cells in the tumor microenvironment are organized, and in colorectal and pancreatic cancer their arrangement around the tumor epithelium carries prognostic information. Multiplexed tissue imaging records the position and phenotype of every cell in a section, and studies of such images now routinely report that two cell types are spatially associated. However, the summaries behind these reports answer different questions. A proximity statistic asks whether two cell types lie close together more often than expected by chance. A conditional network asks whether their local densities rise and fall together once the other cell types are held fixed. The two can disagree, because every cell type is abundant where tissue is cell-dense and because the images of one patient are repeated measurements of that patient. We asked how epithelial and immune cells are organized in two settings: colorectal cancer with a Crohn's-like reaction (CLR) or diffuse inflammatory infiltration (DII), in 140 CODEX images from 35 patients, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) against its precursor, intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN), in 207 multiplex immunofluorescence images from 141 patients. We developed a patient-level analysis that keeps proximity, recurrent local composition and conditional coordination as separate quantities, tests conditional organization as a function of local epithelial density within each section, checks before every conditional estimate that the two cell types are disjoint sets of cells observed together in enough images, and calibrates each conclusion by patient-label permutation, cellularity adjustment under two definitions, spatial-scale perturbation and fully nested leave-one-patient-out prediction. In colorectal cancer, the conditional association between epithelial and myeloid density turned negative with local epithelial density about four times faster in DII than in CLR (difference $-0.0553$ per quartile; 95% CI, $-0.0833$ to $-0.0273$; patient-label familywise $P=0.006$), with no accompanying difference in proximity. In the pancreas, cytotoxic and helper T cells were closer together in PDAC than in IPMN at every scale examined ($q\leq0.023$), whereas their conditional association differed between the two diseases under only one of the two cellularity definitions. Recurrent neighborhoods carried the most patient-level information in colorectal cancer (AUC 0.794) and combined spatial features in the pancreas (AUC 0.771). Pancreatic epithelial--immune and regulatory T-cell quantities could not be estimated from these cores and are reported as such. The analysis is implemented in the R package spatialMIFtools, available at https://github.com/sagnikbhadury/spatialMIFtools.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Epidemiological studies associate replacing animal-sourced with plant-sourced protein with lower colorectal cancer (CRC) risk, but controlled feeding studies have rarely tested how this substitution alters the gut microbiota and CRC-related biomarkers. In a 12-week randomized controlled feeding study, 136 healthy adults consumed diets providing 30 energy percent (E%), 50 E%, or 70 E% of protein from plant sources. Change in gut microbiota composition was the primary outcome; stool characteristics, fecal N-nitroso compounds (NOCs), and fecal and plasma bile acids (BAs) were secondary outcomes. The 70% plant-protein diet significantly restructured the gut microbiota, increasing fiber-associated Lachnospiraceae and Roseburia while reducing Methanobrevibacter and several asaccharolytic taxa. Microbial functional potential shifted toward plant-carbohydrate degradation, with lower amino acid degradation and methanogenesis. Fecal pH decreased, stool characteristics suggested faster colonic transit, and potentially carcinogenic total and haem-derived NOCs declined progressively with plant-protein replacement. The 70% plant-protein diet also reduced fecal secondary and taurine-conjugated BAs, including the CRC-associated BAs DCA and LCA. Plasma glucuronidated BAs increased, expanding the circulating pool of readily excreted BA conjugates. Higher insoluble fiber intake was associated with greater microbiota restructuring and lower fecal NOCs. Methanogen carriers had higher baseline fecal NOCs and features of slower colonic transit, and showed weaker microbiota and less favorable BA responses to the 70% plant-protein diet. Baseline methanogen carriage thus could be exploited for participant stratification in future dietary interventions. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT03206827.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Aneuploidy is a hallmark of colorectal cancer, yet the functional consequences of recurrent chromosome gains and losses remain largely unknown. Leveraging advances in human colon organoid culture and chromosome copy number engineering, we here identify the gain of chromosome 7 as an adaptive event following APC loss-of-function mutation. Trisomy 7 confers a cell-intrinsic fitness advantage to APC-mutant colon organoids, while selective removal of the additional chromosome 7 copy from patient-derived colon cancer organoids severely impairs colorectal cancer organoid growth. By comparing transcriptomes of isogenic disomy 7 and trisomy 7 organoid lines, we found that chromosome 7 gain promotes organoid fitness through attenuation of excessive WNT-driven stemness caused by bi-allelic APC mutation. The gain of chromosome 7 thus establishes a just-right WNT signaling state. This effect of chromosome 7 gain is conserved from early adenoma-like APC-mutant organoids to advanced colorectal cancer organoids carrying additional oncogenic driver mutations. Moreover, consistent with our organoid data, gain of chromosome 7 is particularly common in tumors of colorectal cancer patients whose APC genotypes confer relatively high WNT activity. Overall, this work demonstrates that chromosome-specific aneuploidy can act as an adaptive mechanism to optimize, rather than maximize, oncogenic signaling during tumor evolution.

DNA methylation aberrations and variability are pervasive features of cancer, yet their relationship with chromatin regulation remains incompletely understood. Across hundreds of matched tumor-normal methylomes, regions with the highest methylation entropy in both tumor and normal tissues were consistently enriched for PRC2-associated factors. In tumors, inter-sample methylation variability was increased across the full range of PRC2-associated levels, while mean methylation progressively increased from low- to high-PRC2-binding regions; this gradient was substantially weaker in matched normal tissues. PRC2-associated regions with higher DNA methylation levels were preferentially associated with poised and repressed chromatin states, reduced chromatin accessibility, and reduced gene expression. Independent normal-precancer-cancer cohorts showed that this PRC2-associated methylation state emerges early, with precancerous and malignant tissues displaying highly similar profiles that are distinct from those of healthy tissues. Single-cell colon cancer methylomes independently confirmed increased methylation entropy at PRC2 regions. Higher PRC2-region entropy was associated with scores reflecting hypoxic states, aggressive tumor features, and poorer survival outcomes. Collectively, these findings identify PRC2-binding regions as hotspots of DNA methylation variability that become dysregulated during tumorigenesis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
DNA replication licensing is tightly coordinated with cell-cycle progression to ensure genome stability. Here we demonstrate that CIZ1, a nuclear matrix scaffold protein in human cells, coordinates DNA replication licensing through direct interactions with the Origin Recognition Complex (ORC), CDC6, and Cyclins E/A-CDK2. The C-terminal zinc finger region of CIZ1 mediates binding to the cyclin-binding motifs of ORC1 and CDC6, and Cyclin -CDK-dependent phosphorylation regulates these interactions. Cell cycle analyses demonstrated a dynamic association of CIZ1 with ORC1 and CDC6. Functional studies showed that CIZ1 depletion impaired MCM loading, reduced DNA synthesis, delayed S-phase progression and inhibited cell proliferation. Cancer cells overexpressing CIZ1 exhibited an enhanced dependency on its expression, and CRISPR tiling screens identified the C-terminal regulatory region containing cyclin-binding motifs and CDK phosphorylation sites as essential for cell proliferation. Acute degradation of CIZ1 further revealed an unexpected role in maintaining CCCTC-binding factor (CTCF) occupancy at specific genomic loci and regulating transcriptional programs associated with cell adhesion and migration, indicating that CIZ1 links DNA replication with higher-order genome organization. Finally, depletion of CIZ1 significantly suppressed colorectal tumor growth in xenograft models. Together, these findings establish CIZ1 as a multifunctional scaffold that integrates DNA replication licensing, Cyclin -CDK signaling, and chromatin architecture.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immunotherapy has transformed the management of many cancers, such as clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), yet durable clinical benefit is achieved in only a subset of patients. Immunotherapy outcomes are governed by the multicellular tumor microenvironment (TME), through the structured and directional interplay of regulatory programs and ligand-receptor communications. Yet most existing methods for immunotherapy response prediction rely on independent signatures or cell types and fail to model the structured and directional signaling network within the TME. To address this gap, we introduce EcoNet, a computational framework that first models ecosystems consisting of co-occurring cell states, then constructs intercellular and intracellular signaling networks based on the ecosystems, and applies a graph attention network to derive embeddings from the signaling network for immunotherapy response prediction. Pretrained on 2,532 pan-cancer immunotherapy samples across multiple cohorts, EcoNet outperformed existing prediction methods by 7.5-19.9% and marker-based signatures by 4.4-21.2% in AUC, and its high-attention genes were enriched among those required for T-cell-mediated tumor killing in an independent CRISPR screen; applied to ccRCC with disease-specific fine-tuning, it stratified an independent ccRCC cohort by clinical outcome (P=0.024). Biologically, high-attention genes capture an interferon-responsive program that enhances antigen presentation and immune infiltration. To validate these findings, we curated a ccRCC clinical cohort profiled with CosMx single-cell spatial transcriptomics (46 samples, ~450,000 cells) and found the response-associated TME configuration identified by EcoNet localized to immune-enriched niches, supporting the response stratification. These results establish EcoNet as a generalizable framework for TME-informed therapeutic response prediction, readily extensible to other cancer types and therapeutic contexts.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Genomic stratification leaves most patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) without opportunities for targeted therapy. Seeking tumour state-linked drug sensitivities, we combined image-based ex vivo drug profiling with matched transcriptomics in 127 prospectively collected patient biopsies across CRC stages and molecular subtypes. Network-level integration identified a ciliogenic cell state defined by upregulation of cilia related genes with selective sensitivity to the FGFR inhibitor erdafitinib. This ciliogenic signature was associated with poor progression-free survival (hazard ratio 2.28; adjusted p=0.0098), even in early-stage colorectal cancer. Furthermore, knockdown of the transcriptional regulators RFX2 and RFX3, upstream of the ciliogenic cell state, attenuated erdafitinib sensitivity. Orthogonal bulk and single-cell analyses across normal, primary and metastatic tissues contextualised the ciliogenic programme along a transition from canonical epithelial states towards fetal and non-canonical tumour states, concomitant with Wnt-related remodelling, FGFR1/FGFR2 upregulation, and loss of intestinal epithelial identity. Together, these findings define a tumour-intrinsic ciliogenic cell state as a feature of CRC progression, revealing a patient-stratified repurposing opportunity for targeted therapy beyond the current CRC treatment paradigms.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
BackgroundTotal neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) is increasingly used for treatment of locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) to improve treatment compliance, oncological outcomes and opportunities for organ preservation. However, evidence describing its implementation and outcomes in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. This study evaluated the feasibility, treatment delivery, oncological outcomes and organ preservation outcomes of TNT in a real-world South African setting. MethodsThis was a retrospective review of a prospective cohort of adults with histologically confirmed, non-metastatic LARC treated with TNT at the Wits Donald Gordon Medical Centre, Johannesburg, between March 2022 and January 2026. Treatment was individualised following multidisciplinary review and included induction and/or consolidation systemic chemotherapy with either long- or short-course radiotherapy. Following TNT, treatment response was assessed clinically, endoscopically and radiologically. Patients with a clinical complete response (cCR) were offered watch-and-wait (WW) surveillance, while those with an incomplete response were recommended for total mesorectal excision (TME). The primary outcome was organ preservation, assessed as TME-free survival. Secondary outcomes included tumour regrowth, disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and local recurrence-free survival (LRFS) following TME. ResultsForty-six patients were included; median age was 63 years, 67.4% were male, 82.6% had T3-T4 tumours and 80.4% had node-positive disease. TNT was completed as planned in 95.7% of patients. Grade [≥]3 toxicity occurred in 19.5% during chemotherapy and 8.9% during radiotherapy. Twenty-one patients (45.7%) achieved a cCR and entered WW surveillance. TME-free survival was 46% (95% CI 31-60) at 1-year and 18% (95% CI 8-32) at 3-years. Three-year OS and DFS were 87% (95% CI 64-96) and 76% (95% CI 53-89), respectively. Among patients managed with WW, 3-year regrowth-free survival was 53% (95% CI 26-75). Three-year LRFS following TME was 94% (95% CI 68-99), and all patients undergoing TME or completed salvage surgery achieved an R0 resection. ConclusionTNT was feasible and well tolerated in this real-world South African cohort, with high treatment completion and favourable medium-term oncological outcomes. Although almost half of patients initially achieved a cCR, declining TME-free and regrowth-free survival demonstrated that durable organ preservation was less frequent, highlighting the importance of structured surveillance and timely access to salvage surgery. These findings support the feasibility of delivering contemporary multimodal rectal cancer care in an appropriately resourced African setting.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Decision models like Jev read text and return probabilities, categories, or ordinal levels, with confidence scores for the latter two, at a fraction of large language models (LLMs) cost. We explored how Jev could be integrated into clinical workflows for all these output types: mortality risk estimation, categorical Choosing-Wisely decisions for patient questions, and ordinal colon cancer staging. With standard LLM-style inputs, Jev trailed five flagship LLMs: mortality AUROC was 0.822 versus 0.837-0.846; Choosing-Wisely accuracy, 87.7% versus 98.4-100%; and staging accuracy, 45.4% versus 94.2-100%. Developer-recommended input alterations improved staging accuracy to 75.8% with medical context, 82.1% with task decomposition, and 85.8% with both. None of Jevs staging errors had full confidence. Using Jev for fully confident staging decisions and LLMs for the rest was non-inferior to each LLM alone and cut flagship LLM costs by 33-44%. Prompted as designed, decision models may efficiently share structured clinical tasks with LLMs.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Several inherited predispositions to colorectal cancer exist, most notably familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), which typically involves a germline loss-of-function mutation in one APC allele. A second hit in APC or related loci leads to aberrant Wnt signalling, triggering adenoma formation with near-complete penetrance. Yet, substantial variability in disease onset and severity, even among siblings with identical APC germline mutations, implicates environmental modifiers. Emerging evidence points to the gut microbiome as a critical regulator of adenoma initiation and progression, particularly in early-onset CRC. Here, we show that bacterial invasion is associated with neutrophil immunosuppression, T-cell exclusion and adenoma progression in a porcine model of FAP. Longitudinal mapping of progressing and regressing polyps using single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics and integrated microbiome profiling resolved the cellular and microbial architecture underlying these divergent lesion states. Single-cell RNA-seq identified 35 cell subpopulations and showed that regressing polyps are enriched for central-memory CD4+ T cells, cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and inflammatory neutrophils, whereas progressing polyps contain immunosuppressive/PD-L1-associated neutrophils, regulatory and dysfunctional T cells. Spatial transcriptomics with a custom host panel and targeted bacterial probes linked bacterial-high adenomatous regions to immunosuppressive neutrophil niches and T cell exclusion, while regressing lesions showed predominantly lumen-adjacent bacterial localization and spatially organized immune surveillance. These results provide a spatially resolved map of cellular and microbial organisation in early colorectal polyp progression and regression and reveal a microbiome-driven, neutrophil-mediated mechanism of early tumour progression with implications for CRC interception.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ion channels regulate cell proliferation, survival and migration, but the functional consequences of many ion channel mutations in cancer are unknown, and electrophysiological characterisation at scale is impractical. Here we use the mutational landscape of colorectal adenocarcinoma as a functional filter to identify potassium channel mutations under selection. A dN/dS screen of 16 potassium channels expressed in the large intestine identified KCNA5 (Kv1.5) as the strongest candidate under positive mutational selection. These mutations cluster in the T1 tetramerisation, S1-S4 voltage-sensor and pore domains, yet avoid the selectivity filter, indicating that selection does not favour loss of conduction. Within the pore region, the observed mutations occupy a biophysical space distinct from known C-type inactivation, activation-gate and toxin-binding mutations. In the voltage sensor, mutations affect gating-charge arginines. In the T1 domain, mutations fall on inter-subunit interfaces conserved across the KCNA family, and saturation mutagenesis energy calculations predict that they destabilise subunit contacts or the folding of the domain. Molecular dynamics simulations of D166N and G128R show loss of coordinated interface dynamics and distortion of the local backbone, respectively. Transcriptomic analysis of KCNA5-mutant tumours shows reduced expression of cell-cycle, KRAS-related and inflammatory pathways, and we observe differences between transcriptional effects induced by T1 and S1-S4 domain mutations. These changes are not reproduced by low KCNA5 expression alone, consistent with an effect specific to the mutant protein. Together, these computational results highlight that KCNA5 is under mutational selection in colorectal adenocarcinoma, and that these mutations are likely functional and induce phenotypic effects on tumors.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Surveillance of individuals with Lynch syndrome (LS), who are carriers of heterozygous inactivating mismatch repair (MMR) gene mutations that predispose to colorectal cancer, enables the study of tumour-immune coevolution during tumour initiation. Somatic loss of MMR activity in the LS colon leads to the accrual of cancer driver mutations, and also of neoantigens likely to generate an adaptive immune response. However, the spatial and temporal immune dynamics in colon and peripheral blood are uncharacterised. Here we show that the neoplastic evolution of mismatch repair deficient (MMRd) clones leads to large-scale and sustained reorganisation of the T-cell repertoire in colon and peripheral blood. We performed dense spatiotemporal profiling of T cell receptor (TCR) repertoires from 109 colonic biopsies (11 tumour samples, 98 normal bowel) from seven individuals, with eight matched blood repertoires. We additionally analysed 13 colorectal polyp repertoires from eight participants, 286 cross sectional blood repertoires from 242 participants (198 LS and 44 non-LS) and 52 longitudinal peripheral blood samples from 26 individuals with LS. We detected tumour-associated T cell clones, some of which were widely present in normal bowel tissue and also detectable in peripheral blood. Sequence similarity analysis revealed conserved TCR architectures across tissue compartments and recurrent clustering patterns between patients, that were not present in non-Lynch controls, consistent with convergent MMRd-associated antigen-driven immune selection. We identified systemic signatures associated with local tumour immune activity and revealed evidence of structured repertoire remodelling before overt malignancy. Longitudinal profiling revealed frequent turnover of low-abundance clonotypes, whereas highly abundant clonotypes persisted for several years. Collectively, our data defines the local and circulating TCR landscape associated with colonic neoplasia in LS, and provides a framework for LS blood-based immune monitoring, early interception and biomarker development.

EAES-SAGES临床实践指南更新：憩室病管理关键争议的多学会建议
EAES-SAGES clinical practice guideline update: multi-society recommendations on key controversies in the management of diverticular disease.
Surgical Endoscopy · 2026-10 · Huo B, Al Khaldi M, Shehata D, Calabrese EC, Reinke C, Carrano F, et al.
要点与启示：该指南针对憩室病诊疗争议给出循证推荐，但与结直肠癌及肝转移无直接关联，对肠癌研究启示有限。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We identified areas of controversy in the management of patients with diverticular disease to develop key questions addressing the management of symptomatic uncomplicated diverticular disease (SUDD), uncomplicated diverticulitis, and complicated diverticulitis. We performed a systematic review to identify randomized trials and cohort studies addressing our key questions. Informed by an updated evidence synthesis, an international, multidisciplinary panel of gastrointestinal surgeons, gastroenterologists, patient partners, and methodologists applied the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) evidence-to-decision framework during panel consensus meetings to derive recommendations for the management of patients with diverticular disease. The systematic review identified 27 studies representing very low to moderate certainty evidence. The panel made the following recommendations: 1. In patients with SUDD, we suggest rifaximin or mesalamine over standard supportive care (conditional recommendation); 2. In patients with uncomplicated diverticulitis, we suggest no routine antibiotics (conditional recommendation); 3. In patients with persistent symptoms following an episode of recurrent uncomplicated diverticulitis, we suggest elective resection over observation (conditional recommendation); 4. In patients who have recovered from a first episode of uncomplicated diverticulitis, we suggest no routine follow-up colonoscopy (conditional recommendation); 5. In patients who have recovered from a first episode of diverticulitis complicated by an abscess, we suggest elective resection over surveillance (conditional recommendation). The panel judged that a significant proportion of patients would place a high value in reducing the risk of recurrence at 1 year but also acknowledged the lack of evidence addressing prioritized outcomes including 30-day major complications, need for emergency surgery, stoma-free survival at 1 year, and quality of life at 1 year. Given that patient values and preferences may vary, clinicians are encouraged to apply patient-centered decision-making and discuss the alternatives. This clinical practice guideline update provides evidence-informed recommendations to support patients and clinicians in the management of diverticular disease.

Belgian protocol for indication and selection of patients with unresectable colorectal cancer liver metastases eligible for liver transplantation.

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is common in Western countries, about 50% of patients develop liver metastases (CLM). While local CLM therapies can achieve 5-year survival up to 60%, most patients eventually become unresectable (uCLM) and have poor outcomes with systemic treatment alone. Prospective studies, including SECA I and II and the TransMet trial, showed that in carefully selected patients, liver transplantation (LTx) can achieve survival outcomes comparable to standard LTx indications. The aim of this work was to develop a harmonized national consensus protocol for the indication and selection of uCLM patients eligible for LTx. Under the coordination of the Belgian Liver & Intestine Advisory Committee (Be-LIAC), all six Belgian transplant centers delegated a transplant surgeon, an oncologist and an hepatologist to a working group that performed a literature review and drafted preliminary criteria. Three successive national meetings and a structured voting refined these criteria in the current protocol. Consensus was reached on inclusion and exclusion criteria for LTx in uCLM. Two key conditions are liver-only disease and technically uCLM. Strict requirements include a six months disease stability or response on systemic therapy and an obligatory eight-week treatment holiday. Absolute CEA levels and specific somatic mutations are not excluded. A national Be-LIAC governance model was established, combining local prospective decision-making with central auditing and registry-based evaluation. A harmonized national protocol for LTx inuCLM has been established, ensuring consistent patient selection across all Belgian centers. Stricter criteria and a national governance model aim to optimize outcomes while maintaining ethical allocation of donor organs.

本周热点与趋势总结

由本期文献提炼的课题组可执行信号
  1. 肝转移机制与代谢-表观调控：Cancer Letters 报道，对患者配对的正常黏膜、原发结直肠癌与肝转移灶进行定量蛋白质组与赖氨酸2-羟基异丁酰化（Khib）修饰组学分析，发现整体Khib水平沿“正常→原发→肝转移”逐步升高，并富集于RNA剪接蛋白；剪接因子SRSF9及其K155位点Khib修饰随疾病进展上调，通过调控CD44可变剪接促进结直肠癌肝转移。该研究将代谢修饰重塑与转移性RNA剪接程序直接联系，提示Khib/SRSF9-CD44轴是肝转移潜在干预靶点。
  2. 肝转移与肿瘤微环境/免疫治疗：Nature Immunology 揭示脂质感应转录因子PPARδ具有区室特异性——在癌细胞中激活促进生长并削弱抗肿瘤免疫，而在免疫细胞（尤其CD8+ T细胞）中激活则驱动肿瘤抑制并可逆转癌细胞内在激活的促瘤效应，从而决定免疫治疗疗效。该“癌症-免疫适能平衡”框架为解释MSS型结直肠癌免疫耐药及联合策略（含肝转移灶免疫微环境重塑）提供了新思路。
  3. 微生物组与肠癌发生及免疫治疗增效：Cell Host & Microbe 同期发表两项重要研究。其一，Gm（Gemella morbillorum）在结直肠癌患者粪便与肿瘤组织中富集，通过抑制ILC3来源IL-22破坏肠屏障、促使细菌易位至早期瘤变部位，并以ANXA2依赖、网格蛋白介导的入侵引发DNA损伤，构成多步骤促瘤机制；其二，口服Akkermansia muciniphila通过TLR2/NF-κB通路减弱巨噬细胞胞葬作用，导致凋亡癌细胞蓄积并激活cGAS-STING-I型干扰素通路，从而增强MSS结直肠癌抗PD-1疗效。两项研究共同支持“细菌-屏障-免疫”轴作为MSS肠癌免疫增敏的可转化方向。
  4. RAS通路突变的多组学重塑与微生态反馈：Cell Communication and Signaling 利用同源HCT116与RKO模型进行ATAC-seq，显示KRAS/BRAF突变驱动染色质可及性与转录程序重编程，界定RAS通路突变（约占CRC 40%）的表观调控网络；Cell Host & Microbe 同期评论指出突变KRAS偏好Bacteroides acidifaciens，后者经SusF-ARHGEF2轴反向强化RAS-MAPK信号，形成“基因-微生物”正反馈。二者提示RAS分型肠癌的染色质重塑与菌群互作可能共同决定靶向治疗耐受。
  5. 治疗策略与支持治疗证据升级：Cancer Treatment Reviews 系统综述将运动从生活方式建议提升为潜在抗癌干预：逾140万参与者的汇总分析显示规律活动与至少13种肿瘤发病风险降低相关，前瞻队列中乳腺癌、结直肠癌、前列腺癌与肺癌最活跃患者肿瘤特异性死亡低24–31%（观察性、自报活动数据）；2025年III期试验在III期结肠癌中首次提供随机对照证据。同期Nature Medicine 基于52,236例MSK-IMPACT纵向数据构建健康系统尺度、按发作解析的癌症恶病质多模态图谱，显示恶病质发作聚集于疾病进展期并与几乎所有癌种的不良结局相关，为肠癌进展期营养-代谢干预与试验终点设计提供量化框架。
  6. AI辅助分期与诊断转化：Advanced Science 提出多中心基础模型DeepLNM，整合H&E全切片图像、CT与文本多模态数据预测结直肠癌淋巴结转移，内部队列平均AUC达0.922，并经回顾性、外部、前瞻性及用户研究多层级验证。该工作针对影像与常规病理假阴/假阳的临床痛点，提示多模态AI有望优化肠癌（含肝转移候选者）术前分期与治疗选择。
